title: A's Prospect Devin Taylor Has a Bat That Can Play Now, But No Clear Path
description: The A's outfielder prospect is hitting .347 in Double-A with a case for Vegas, but defensive limitations and a crowded outfield loom. Manager Mark Kotsay breaks down the timeline.
fullText:
One A's prospect that could find himself in Las Vegas shortly is outfielder Devin Taylor, who manager Mark Kotsay said he's arguably the team's best bat in the minor leagues. MLB Pipeline has him ranked No. 6 in the A's system in just his first full season.

After being selected by the Athletics in the second round of the 2025 MLB Draft out of Indiana, and the early assessment of him was that his bat could play immediately, but his glove was a work in progress.

In his first full professional season, Taylor was assigned to High-A Lansing to begin the year, where he hit .292 with a .425 OBP and an .861 OPS, adding six home runs in 57 games. Taylor was promoted to Double-A Midland on June 9, and in 47 games he has hit .347 with a .407 OBP and a .973 OPS, adding 10 home runs.

He's hitting for average and power and is making a strong case to reach the next level before the season is over. He's started August going 8-for-18 (.444) and has hit above .300 in each month in Midland.

The big question thus far has been his defensive ability, which could be the factor that keeps him in the minors a little longer. Given those early reports on him, Athletics Roundtable decided to ask Kotsay about Taylor last week.

MLB Pipeline and FanGraphs view his defensive ability very differently. FanGraphs has his fielding rated as a 20 on the 20-80 scout scale, which is as bad as it gets. Pipeline has him at a 45, which still isn't great, but that's a playable glove. We asked about his defense, but first Kotsay wanted to gush about his bat.

"Obviously [bench coach] Darren Bush has told me all about him and filled me in on how much he likes [Taylor's] swing," Kotsay said. "He's dropped some weight, he's gotten a little more athletic, so I think that's helped his defense. I know that it's a priority to improve his defense. I think there's still a lot of growth in there."

Taylor played mostly left field in college, but has been splitting some time between left and right field this year. In Midland, he's seen more time in right, getting into 24 there and 17 in left.

He could be a DH type that moves quickly through the system, but the A's already have Brent Rooker locked in at that spot, while Tyler Soderstrom and Lawrence Butler patrol left and right fields. All three of those players have signed extensions, which complicates Taylor's path to the big leagues.

The A's aren't a team that likes to promote players straight from Midland to the big leagues. They believe in checking off boxes at every level. Yet, after the club played regular season games in Las Vegas back in June, some eyes were opened to the challenges that Las Vegas Ballpark presents.

We asked about the potential of advancing pitchers straight from Midland to Sacramento, skipping Vegas and the trauma that would come with it, and the response wasn't a flat no, but that the organization still believes in having Triple-A be a development step for pitchers, with them having to go through some adversity.

With Taylor blasting off, we asked Kotsay if the club would consider advancing a bat — not necessarily Taylor, just more general — with the thought process of not wanting to get this hitter to develop bad routines and tendencies because how easily the ball flies at Vegas Ballpark.

"I think the key factors with development are trying to get every player at a level where they experience some failure," Kotsay said. "I think there's some separation between the big leagues and Triple-A in terms of performance and the way that it translates right now.

He added that he didn't want to say that it's not a possibility, but sometimes a hitter benefits from going to a hitter's park and gaining that confidence.

"I don't think that they'll do anything differently to change the way they attack the baseball from Double-A to Triple-A," Kotsay continued. "Whether the ball stays in the air longer, the foundation is built by the time they get there in terms of how they approach the zone and what their swing path is. But if they do, then there's obviously indicators that we'll we'll see and be able to make adjustments."

While it's unlikely he finds himself on the A's roster this season, Kotsay says that it's important for a prospect to face some adversity. Thus far he hasn't faced any in High-A or Double-A this season, which likely leads to a promotion to Las Vegas in the coming weeks to give him a look at the level before the end of the season.

title: Mets’ Jefry Yan has the perfect reaction to 1st MLB strikeout
description: Jefry Yan waited more than a decade for his first MLB strikeout, and his celebration made sure everyone knew it.
fullText:
Mets' Jefry Yan has the perfect reaction to 1st MLB strikeout appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Jefry Yan waited a long time for this moment, and he made sure to enjoy every second of it. The Mets reliever recorded the first strikeout of his major league career Wednesday night against the Cleveland Guardians, freezing pinch hitter Angel Martinez on an 88.7 mph slider in the sixth inning of New York's eventual 6-5 win.

Asked afterward to grade the execution of his signature celebration, Yan did not hold back.

"I went out there to attack him. Once I had him at two strikes, I said, you know what, I'm going to throw that slider," Yan said. "And if I freeze him, which is exactly what I did, I celebrated accordingly."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"If I freeze him, which is exactly what I did, I celebrated accordingly."

Jefry Yan was asked to rate the execution of his first MLB strikeout celebration: pic.twitter.com/zKG2ihwLKY

— SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 6, 2026

The celebration itself lived up to the hype that had followed Yan for years. He leaped high into the air with his feet spread apart, landed on the front of the mound, slapped the grass with his left hand, and briefly dropped to a knee before rising with both arms raised overhead. Cleveland fans booed him off the mound, a reaction Yan said did not bother him in the slightest.

"Honestly, I don't think about that," Yan said. "They can do whatever they want there. They're paying their tickets, so if they want to yell at me, if they want to boo me, they can do whatever they want. I'm in my zone, and I'm going to enjoy my game any way that I want to."

Yan's path to this moment took over a decade. Originally signed by the Los Angeles Angels out of the Dominican Republic in 2014, he spent years bouncing around the minors, including a stretch working as a roofer in Arizona to make ends meet, before a stint in Japan and later Colorado's system.

He signed a minor league deal with the Mets last August and was called up from Triple-A Syracuse on Monday, finally debuting at age 29 with the same electric celebration that had already made him a viral sensation in spring training.

Interim manager Andy Green praised the moment for what it represented beyond just the strikeout itself.

"It's real stuff. It's really impressive. To get out of a bases-loaded jam, get your first punchout, just excited for him. He deserves that," Green said.

title: Liverpool edge closer to confirming £72m deal
description: Liverpool have been at the centre of attention for some time now. Before the 2026-27 summer transfer window even opened, the Anfield outfit were expected to undergo many changes throughout their ranks...
fullText:
Liverpool have been at the centre of attention for some time now.

Before the 2026-27 summer transfer window even opened, the Anfield outfit were expected to undergo many changes throughout their ranks.

Several areas among their first-team squad needed upgrading which is what led many fans to believe that another rebuild was on its way.

However, thanks to many different things, that has been far from the case and now, it feels like the Reds are in limbo.

Many members of their first-team squad are being linked with moves away and, since there's only around a month left of the transfer window, decisions on the future of those players will need to be made as soon as possible.

One of the main areas that Liverpool are going to struggle reinforcing this summer is their attack.

Hugo Ekitike is out of action until at least January and, with Mohamed Salah now a Trabzonspor player, it's clear that a replacement for the Egyptian King will need to be signed.

Many attackers have been linked with a move to Liverpool but, the vast majority of them seem to be left-wingers, rather than right-wingers.

In the grand scheme of things, this isn't much of an issue as versatility is one of the key aspects of a players game now but, if they want someone to hit the ground running and fill Salah's void, they need a natural right-winger among their ranks.

So, with all of this in mind, the fact that Cody Gakpo would become Bradley Barcola's back-up if Liverpool signed him this season isn't all that surprising.

"Bradley Barcola would be signed to play left wing for Liverpool, not the Salah replacement," Anfield Sector shared via X.

"He would come in ahead of Cody Gakpo in the pecking order should a deal be agreed with PSG, with negotiations progressing slowly but the PSG hierarchy currently unwilling to compromise on a €150m+ valuation."

During the 2024-25 season, Gakpo was one of Liverpool's best attackers.

The left-winger was fighting with Luis Diaz for a starting role and had one of his best-ever seasons as a Liverpool player.

And, even though he started the 2025-26 season off as Liverpool's only left-winger, he somehow got worse and was terrible for most of the campaign.

This led to fans demanding that Rio Ngumoha started over the Dutchman and, in the end, Slot gave in and allowed to youngster to start a few games.

From that point on, links with several left-wingers have emerged and, of the lot, it's clear that Barcola would be the best option.

Not only did he contribute to 20 goals across all competitions last term but, he also played across the front three which makes him a lot more versatile than Gakpo.

There are obviously still a lot of moving parts that could affect the deal but, if Liverpool can swap Gakpo for Barcola, it's a move that they should definitely sanction.

title: Olympic ski champion Gut-Behrami has ended career
description: Olympic and twice world champion champion Lara Gut-Behrami of Switzerland will not return to alpine skiing from a severe knee injury and has ended her career. Gut-Behrami, 35, told broadcasters RSI on Wednesday evening she had "the honour to experience a long career, to express my wishes and dreams through my skiing and to experience this journey alongside extraordinary people.
fullText:
Olympic and twice world champion champion Lara Gut-Behrami of Switzerland will not return to alpine skiing from a severe knee injury and has ended her career.

Gut-Behrami, 35, told broadcasters RSI on Wednesday evening she had "the honour to experience a long career, to express my wishes and dreams through my skiing and to experience this journey alongside extraordinary people."

Gut-Behrami wanted to ski a final season in 2025-26 with the Milan/Cortina Olympics but suffered a ruptured cruciate and medial collateral ligament as well as a torn meniscus in a training accident in November 2025.

The injury sidelined her for the season and she left it open at the time whether she would add a final campaign in 2026-27.

"Despite 20 years of elite sport, crashes and injuries I have had no recurring pain and don't want to have it. For that reason as well I have the feeling that the right moment has come - the moment when I no longer have to insist, at all costs, on reaching and exceeding my limits," she said.

Gut-Behrami made her World Cup debut in 2007 and won 48 races. She won the overall World Cup twice, in 2016 and 2024, and seven discipline titles, six in super-g and one in giant slalom.

She won the super-g and giant slalom at the 2021 world championships and Olympic super-g gold a year later. In all, she has 12 medals from worlds and Olympics.

title: New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote After Loss to Cardinals
description: Yankees manager Aaron Boone dropped a blunt quote after New York's loss to the St. Louis Cardinals on Wednesday. The post New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote After Loss to Cardinals appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees lost to the St. Louis Cardinals 3-1 at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday night, completing the three-game series. St. Louis won the first game 13-7, and New York won the second 2-0.

In the finale, the Yankees went 0-for-10 with runners in scoring position. Manager Aaron Boone dropped a blunt quote on the team's inability to come through in big situations during the game.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 29: Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks back to the dugout during the fourth inning against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on June 29, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images)

"We got to get it done. We got to come through in those situations," Boone said (via YES Network). "Like the opportunities tonight. Had a lot of chances, felt like baserunners every inning, but we got to be able to deliver, and we haven't done that enough."

The game remained scoreless through the first four innings. The Cardinals scored all three of their runs in the top of the fifth, as JJ Wetherholt hit a two-run double and Ivan Herrera followed with an RBI double.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 05: JJ Wetherholt #26 of the St. Louis Cardinals reacts to a 2-run RBI double during the fifth inning against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium on August 05, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)

Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked with the bases loaded in the bottom of the sixth to put the Yankees on the board.

Will Warren made the start for the Yankees. He allowed three earned runs on seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 05: Will Warren #29 of the New York Yankees pitches during the first inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on August 05, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)

Paul Blackburn threw 1 2/3 scoreless innings out of the bullpen. Kervin Castro and Tim Hill each threw a scoreless inning.

For St. Louis, Andrew Pallante earned the win after allowing one run on three hits and three walks with four strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. George Soriano, Justin Bruihl, Ryne Stanek and Riley O'Brien combined for 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 04: George Lombard Jr. #96 of the New York Yankees celebrates with teammates after the ninth inning of his MLB debut against the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on August 04, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. The Yankees won 2-0. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The Yankees are off on Thursday. After that, the team will host the Atlanta Braves for a three-game series this weekend.

New York owns the first American League Wild Card spot. The team is just one game ahead of the second Wild Card team, the Boston Red Sox. As for the division standings, the Yankees are 4 1/2 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the American League East.

title: Nick Nurse smartly responds to Kevin Durant’s viral 76ers-Warriors comparison
description: Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse responds to Kevin Durant’s take on the team. The 2026-27 NBA season is yet to begin, but Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has already hailed the Philadelphia 76ers as the team to beat.
fullText:
Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse responds to Kevin Durant's take on the team.

The 2026-27 NBA season is yet to begin, but Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has already hailed the Philadelphia 76ers as the team to beat.

Additionally, KD compared the current 76ers roster to the iconic 2016-17 Golden State Warriors team and asked the fans to treat them similarly. After all, the 2016-17 Warriors were considered unfair.

Since KD's comments, Draymond Green and Klay Thompson have been very vocal, and now 76ers head coach Nick Nurse has joined the conversation.

Nurse essentially downplayed the comparison during an interview with NBC Sports Philadelphia.

"Championship teams have a lot of similar characteristics," Nurse said. "And the first thing is, is we need to get to work, right? I really still put hard work and work ethic and all that stuff at the top of the list if you want to win."

He added, "Are we going to outwork our opponents, right? Are we going to watch better film, more film, spend more hours?"

In a way, Nurse agreed with Durant, but also pointed out that no matter how talented a roster is, it won't win the NBA Championship without an elite work ethic.

title: OG Anunoby teams up with London’s Mayor to refurbish basketball courts where he was born
description: New York Knicks forward and championship hero OG Anunoby returned to his birthplace in London, for a noble cause. Anunoby, with assistance from the NBPA, has teamed up with London Mayor Sadiq Khan to help improve public basketball infrastructure in his birthplace.
fullText:
New York Knicks forward and championship hero OG Anunoby returned to his birthplace in London, for a noble cause.

Anunoby, with assistance from the NBPA, has teamed up with London Mayor Sadiq Khan to help improve public basketball infrastructure in his birthplace.

Anunoby was born in Harlesden, London, and lived there until he was four years old before his family moved to Missouri, where he pursued his basketball career.

Mayor Khan revealed that his government will team up with Anunoby to refurbish and create public basketball courts for Londoners to use, helping aspiring English hoopers.

"Could this court produce the next NBA player? Every great player starts somewhere. Nobody starts in the NBA; they start somewhere like this."

Anunoby's comments are interspersed with Mayor Khan revealing that the government is investing in refurbishing public courts to give Londoners a chance to reach their potential as basketball players.

The court in the video is the Argyle Square basketball court in Camden, London, and is the first of a pilot project under the Mayor of London's London Basketball Taskforce.

The Mayor had announced a nearly £2 million basketball investment in January 2026 before the NBA London Games, and this court program is part of that commitment.

Anunoby has become a beacon to British-born basketball players with his achievements at the highest level, winning the 2026 NBA Championship with the New York Knicks.

Anunoby averaged 16.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.6 steals in the season and 20.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals, and 1.1 blocks in the Playoffs, emerging as a fan-favorite for his relentless two-way play.

The Knicks are looking to become the first team in nine seasons to defend their crown as NBA Champions, which won't be easy after the moves around the NBA this season.

Anunoby is arguably the greatest English basketball player ever, ranking ahead of the likes of Luol Deng, Ben Gordon, and James Donaldson.

title: Tyler Herro dubs him being traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo the 'craziest' of the offseason
description: It appears Tyler Herro is still not best pleased with the Miami Heat for trading him to land Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Heat gave up Herro, along with Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr.
fullText:
It appears Tyler Herro is still not best pleased with the Miami Heat for trading him to land Giannis Antetokounmpo.

The Heat gave up Herro, along with Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., and Kasparas Jakucionis to bring the Greek Freak to South Beach.

Herro, who is a Milwaukee native, gets the chance to play for his home team. However, it doesn't sound like the star is too happy about the way the deal went down.

One fan in Las Vegas for the NBA Summer League asked several NBA players what they thought was the craziest trade of the offseason.

Herro didn't hesitate to name his own trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo, not offering much explanation outside of the bombshell nature of the move.

Herro wasn't the only one to name this trade, as Jake LaRavia, Nate Ament, and Mike Miller gave the same answer when asked by the fan.

However, other players, like Quentin Grimes, Baron Davis, and JD Davidson, named the Philadelphia 76ers' trading for Jaylen Brown as the craziest move.

Many have described the 2026 offseason as one of the wildest and most chaotic offseasons since 2019, when Kawhi Leonard, Anthony Davis, Paul George, Russell Westbrook, Kevin Durant, and Kyrie Irving all switched teams, completely reshaping the landscape of the NBA.

While the moves this year haven't been quite as impactful, with many of the top contenders in the West still staying relatively the same, the massive names on the move this year have led people to be extremely excited for the new season.

The Eastern Conference definitely has new championship contenders, with both the Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat now expected to challenge the New York Knicks' attempt to go back-to-back.

The 76ers are perhaps the team with the most expectations placed on them, given the improved quality of their starting five after landing LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

Many fans are expecting the 76ers to finally end their 26-year streak and reach the Eastern Conference Finals and possibly the NBA Finals for the first time since 2001.

However, the reigning NBA champions will not make it easy for them, as the New York Knicks will want to get the most out of their current championship core before they are forced to go their separate ways due to the NBA's salary constraints.

title: Outrage as Ugandan football captain beaten to death in street gang attack
description: The 27-year-old was killed by suspected robbers after resisting an attempt to rob him, police say.
fullText:
Ugandans are mourning the death at 27 of one of the country's best-known footballers after he was beaten by suspected robbers near his home in the capital, Kampala.

Police said David Owori was fatally assaulted after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings, prompting an outpouring of grief and renewed public anger over violent crime in Uganda.

Owori captained Sports Club (SC) Villa, the Uganda Premier League record champions, where he played both as a right-back and midfielder. He also represented the country's national team - the Cranes.

"We have lost more than a player - we have lost a leader, brother and friend," SC Villa said in a statement.

Witnesses said a group of attackers hit the footballer with paving stones on Tuesday night before robbing Owori of his belongings and fleeing, leaving him unconscious.

SC Villa spokesperson Asan Kasingye told journalists that Owori was targeted just outside his home in Makindye, a Kampala suburb.

"The player was ambushed by thugs as he approached his home, leaving him with life-threatening injuries before he was rushed to the medical facility," Kasingye said.

Owori was rushed to a nearby medical clinic and then transferred to a private facility in the city, but he died of his injuries on Wednesday.

Local police spokesperson Rachael Kawala said detectives were pursuing leads to identify those responsible.

"The scene of the incident has been documented and processed to ensure that all relevant evidence is collected and preserved," Kawala added.

Owori's murder has sent shockwaves across Uganda, with the football community, including fans and teammates, and politicians demanding justice.

Tributes are continuing to pour in for the defender, who was popularly known as Colgate.

The Federation of Uganda Football Associations (Fufa) described Owori as "a true leader on and off the pitch".

"David was not just a footballer. He was both a leader and an inspiration to a generation," it said in a statement.

The national side, the Cranes, said the team had lost a football star who "carried the hopes" of Uganda.

Parliament on Wednesday observed a minute's silence in honour of Owori and called for a quick investigation.

The versatile player, renowned for his tactical discipline and ability to feature across midfield, returned to SC Villa in 2023 for a second spell, becoming one of the club's longest-serving players.

He helped lead the high-profile team to their first league title in 20 years securing a record 17th top-flight crown in 2024.

His influence on and off the pitch earned him a contract extension until January 2027 with the team.

Owori also featured in the national team during the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign and was regarded as a strong contender for future call-ups to the Cranes.

His death has triggered anger on social media, with many Ugandans questioning the level of violent crime in Kampala and calling for tougher action against criminals.

The killing comes just weeks after the death of another Ugandan sports star - rugby international Sydney Gongodyo - who was also fatally attacked by a mob in Kampala

title: Voice-cloned video falsely claims NBA coach planned to recruit late Filipino basketball player
description: T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. AFP found that the clip had been digitally altered, while the original video was published before Baterbonia's death.
fullText:
T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. AFP found that the clip had been digitally altered, while the original video was published before Baterbonia's death.

"OKC Thunder coach planned to recruit Rene Baterbonia after seeing his potential during his basketball games," the overlaid Tagalog-language text on a TikTok clip reads.

The post has racked up over 869,000 views since it was published on July 20. It claims Baterbonia "would've been the first pure Filipino to join the NBA".

The TikTok video shows Mark Daigneault, head coach of the NBA's Oklahoma City Thunder (OKC Thunder), speaking at a press conference ( archived link).

Daigneault can be heard saying they planned to draft Baterbonia, an 18-year-old college student at Ateneo De Manila University, before he died (archived here and here).

"Over the past year, our scouts closely followed Rene Baterbonia and were impressed by his talent, work ethic, and potential," he appears to say in the clip.

"Internally, we were preparing to select him in the 2026 to 2027 NBA draft and had even discussed a multi-year contract worth approximately 25 million US dollars."

"Unfortunately, events took an unexpected turn, and those plans will never become real."

Social media users shared the same clip on TikTok and Facebook, after Baterbonia and teammate Divine Adili drowned during a team-building exercise in the eastern Philippines on June 8 ( archived link).

Their deaths and the subsequent investigation by authorities unleashed a frenzy of social media posts about Baterbonia, a promising small-town athlete recently recruited into collegiate basketball.

Officials from his hometown of Talacogon in Mindanao island released a statement on July 30, asking the public to stop soliciting financial assistance for the Baterbonia family and to stop posting visits to the basketball player's grave for content ( archived link).

But this video has been altered and the original YouTube video was published on May 31, eight days before Baterbonia's death.

A reverse image search using the clip's keyframes found the original unedited version of the video published on the OKC Thunder's official YouTube channel ( archived link).

The video's description reads: "Head Coach Mark Daigneault speaks with the media at end-of-season interviews."

Daigneault made no mention of Baterbonia in the entirety of the video.

A close inspection of the altered footage found that Daigneault's mouth did not match the audio.

Using the Hiya detection tool within the Verification Plugin found the clip's audio was "very likely AI-generated".

title: Everton complete the signing of Premier League midfielder
description: Everton sign Christian Norgaard as David Moyes reshapes midfieldEverton have moved to strengthen their engine room with the signing of Christian Norgaard from Arsenal on a two-year contract, in a deal...
fullText:
Everton have moved to strengthen their engine room with the signing of Christian Norgaard from Arsenal on a two-year contract, in a deal reported by BBC Sport to be worth £7m. The 32-year-old Denmark international arrives with a clear brief, add control, leadership and reliability to a squad that has needed reinforcement in central areas.

Norgaard made 20 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal last season, although only seven came in the Premier League as they secured their first title in 22 years. His absence from the squad for the recent friendly against Real Betis had already pointed towards an imminent exit, and Everton have now completed the move.

From Everton's perspective, the logic is easy to follow. David Moyes has been seeking experience after the departures of Seamus Coleman and Idrissa Gueye, while James Garner is set to miss the start of the season following groin surgery. In that context, Norgaard looks like a practical solution rather than a speculative one.

The midfielder arrives after a year in north London and before that built an excellent reputation across six seasons at Brentford, where he captained the side and made 196 appearances. He knows the Premier League well and should need little adaptation time.

Norgaard said he was "very intrigued" about the project after speaking to Moyes, adding: "Coming here just makes that feeling even stronger." He also said: "I think the club is moving in the right direction and last year was proof of that. I thought there were so many good players in the team and Everton was so difficult to play against."

Everton have also brought in Hayden Hackney for £16.5m and Tyrique George for £18m, suggesting a blend of youth and experience in this window. Norgaard may not be the headline-grabbing addition, but he fills a need and gives Moyes a player capable of steadying the team in and out of possession.

From an Everton perspective, this feels sensible, but hardly stirring. Norgaard is an experienced professional and there is obvious value in signing someone who understands the Premier League, especially with Gueye gone and Garner unavailable. Still, it is difficult to pretend this is the sort of signing that transforms the mood around the club.

At £7m, the fee is not outrageous, and there is every chance he proves useful over two years. Yet Everton supporters have seen enough short-term fixes to know that competence alone does not always move a team forward. If Moyes wants energy, discipline and leadership, Norgaard should help. If the aim is to lift the ceiling of this midfield, there may still be work to do.

The more encouraging point is what this says about squad planning. Hackney represents the future, George adds another attacking option, and Norgaard covers an immediate need. That mix matters. Even so, there is a lingering sense that Everton are once again shopping for stability rather than ambition. Maybe that is necessary right now, but fans will want to see signs of something more before getting too excited.

title: WTC Points Table: How Pakistan's win over West Indies changed the standings
description: Australia remain at the top of the World Test Championship standings. They have won seven of their eight matches, lost one, collected 84 points and have the best Points Percentage (PCT) of 87.50. Pakistan climbed to eighth after their win over the West Indies. They have won two and lost four of their six matches.
fullText:
Pakistan climbed one place in the World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 points table after beating the West Indies by eight wickets in the second Test in Trinidad. The win helped Pakistan level the two-match series 1-1 and move above the West Indies in the standings.

Earlier, Pakistan had slipped to the bottom of the table after losing the opening Test. They now have two wins from six matches and a points percentage (PCT) of 22.22.

Pakistan also ended their eight-match away losing streak in Test cricket with the victory.

Chasing a target of 77, Pakistan reached 77/2 shortly after lunch on Day 4. Abdullah Shafique, who scored a century in the first innings, remained unbeaten on 24 along with captain Babar Azam, who also finished on 24 not out.

Babar sealed the win by hitting back-to-back sixes off left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican.

West Indies had won the first Test by 90 runs in Tarouba, but Pakistan bounced back strongly in the second match. Spinners Sajid Khan and Ali Usman made the most of the conditions at Queen's Park Oval as Pakistan remained unbeaten in a Test series against the West Indies since 2000.

1. Australia (1st): Australia remain at the top of the World Test Championship standings. They have won seven of their eight matches, lost one, collected 84 points and have the best Points Percentage (PCT) of 87.50.

2. South Africa (2nd): South Africa are second with three wins and one defeat in four matches. They have 36 points and a PCT of 75.00.

3. New Zealand (3rd): New Zealand are third after winning four of their six Tests. They have one loss and one draw, with 52 points and a PCT of 72.22.

4. Bangladesh (4th): Bangladesh occupy fourth place. They have won two matches, lost one and drawn one from four Tests. They have 28 points and a PCT of 58.33.

5. India (5th): India are fifth in the standings. The Shubman Gill-led side have played nine matches, winning four, losing four and drawing one. India have 52 points and a PCT of 48.15.

6. Sri Lanka (6th): Sri Lanka are sixth with one win, one loss and two draws in four matches. They have 20 points and a PCT of 41.67.

7. England (7th): England are seventh after playing 13 matches. They have won four, lost eight and drawn one. England have 38 points and a PCT of 24.36.

8. Pakistan (8th): Pakistan climbed to eighth after their win over the West Indies. They have won two and lost four of their six matches. Pakistan have 16 points and a PCT of 22.22.

9. West Indies (9th): The West Indies slipped to the bottom of the table after the defeat to Pakistan. They have won two, lost eight and drawn two of their 12 matches. They have 30 points and a PCT of 20.83.

title: Jaissle will 'address things head-on'
description: Matthias Jaissle has quite an act to follow at Newcastle United.  Just like Newcastle's moves to sign young players from the continent, there is an element of risk with this appointment as the club bring in a manager who has never coached in the Premier League before.  Jaissle delivered success in Saudi Arabia and Austria - with Al-Ahli and Red Bull Salzburg respectively - but this will be the first time he has sampled life in one of Europe's top five leagues.
fullText:
Matthias Jaissle has quite an act to follow at Newcastle United. As a source said: "It won't be easy to succeed Eddie Howe."

Just like Newcastle's moves to sign young players from the continent, there is an element of risk with this appointment as the club bring in a manager who has never coached in the Premier League before.

Jaissle delivered success in Saudi Arabia and Austria - with Al-Ahli and Red Bull Salzburg respectively - but this will be the first time he has sampled life in one of Europe's top five leagues.

He becomes the Premier League's second-youngest current head coach at 38 years old, and his first competitive game is against Liverpool on Sunday, 23 August.

There has been no time to waste since he arrived at the club's pre-season training camp in Spain at the weekend.

"He will try to understand the culture and what Newcastle means to the community as soon as possible," added a source. "That's what he will live by."

Howe certainly set the standard, however last season was a bruising one domestically.

The club now need a progressive manager to start a new cycle and build on what he did at the peak of his reign.

Effectively, Jaissle's remit will be to develop players and outperform clubs with bigger wage bills - and the squad should expect him to be just as demanding as his predecessor in training.

"We did lots of small-sided games to keep the intensity high," said former Salzburg midfielder Zlatko Junuzovic. "If someone had not been giving it their all, he called them out on it. He isn't afraid to address things head-on."

He also brings with him a group of coaches and analysts who will look to quickly get his message across - Al-Ahli defender Merih Demiral knows that better than most.

"They paid great attention to every detail and always made sure we were fully prepared," Demiral said. "He has built a really strong team around him and they played a huge role in our success."

title: 'I believe there is enormous potential' - Jaissle appointed Newcastle boss
description: New head coach Matthias Jaissle says he "fully and unreservedly" believes in the Newcastle United project.  The club have confirmed the 38-year-old's immediate appointment following the departure of Eddie Howe last month.  Jaissle joins from Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he lead the club to back-to-back AFC Champions League title, having previously been in charge at RB Salzburg for two seasons, securing the Austrian Bundesliga twice and also the Austrian Cup once.
fullText:
New head coach Matthias Jaissle says he "fully and unreservedly" believes in the Newcastle United project.

The club have confirmed the 38-year-old's immediate appointment following the departure of Eddie Howe last month.

Jaissle joins from Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he lead the club to back-to-back AFC Champions League title, having previously been in charge at RB Salzburg for two seasons, securing the Austrian Bundesliga twice and also the Austrian Cup once.

Speaking to club media, Jaissle said: "It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United. This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

"When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice. The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be. I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see.

"I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking. There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.

"My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day. I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions.

"I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward.

"I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

The German will get straight to work with the side, who face Valencia in a pre-season friendly on Saturday, with his coaching team to be announced shortly.

David Hopkinson, Newcastle United CEO, said on the appointment: "Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I'm thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United.

"We have conducted a thorough process, and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role. He possesses all the qualities we were looking for.

"His track record of success, leadership qualities and relentless drive to improve make him an exceptional fit for Newcastle United. We believe he is the right person to lead the club into the next phase of our journey."

title: 3 Things That Make Mamuka Usubyan A Serious Problem For Marat Grigorian At The Inner Circle 25
description: His ONE SAMURAI Featherweight Kickboxing Tournament clash goes down in Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on August 7.
fullText:
Mamuka Usubyan has quietly built one of the most dangerous runs in the featherweight kickboxing division, and no opponent in ONE Championship has found an answer for it yet.

Next, the Russian standout collides with three-time Glory Kickboxing World Champion Marat Grigorian at The Inner Circle 25 in a quarterfinal matchup of the ONE SAMURAI Featherweight Kickboxing Tournament.

The card will stream live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's iconic Lumpinee Stadium this Friday, August 7, and will be available only for members at live.onefc.com.

Grigorian is not lacking confidence heading into this high-stakes clash, but the man standing across from him brings just as much poise, including a 24-2 resume that includes scalps over former World Champions.

Before the two collide, here are three things that make Usubyan a genuine problem for the Armenian knockout artist.

Usubyan has never once been knocked out in his career, and his iron chin has been on full display across four fights in the world's largest martial arts organization.

Three of those victories came against fighters who have made careers out of putting opponents to sleep: Rajadamnern Stadium Muay Thai World Champions Shadow Mavinn and Khunsuek Superbon Training Camp, and ISKA Kickboxing World Champion Enzo Kartoum.

All three arrived with legitimate knockout pedigree and every intention of adding Usubyan's name to their highlight reels. None of them managed it as the Russian extended his active win streak to seven – a run that stretches back to July 2023.

That kind of chin could prove enormously frustrating for Grigorian. The Armenian, a 70-win veteran, rarely misses when he opens fire, and few men have ever been able to stand in front of him without eventually crumbling.

Usubyan's jaw, though, has yet to find its breaking point, and there is no reason to believe that changes at The Inner Circle 25 this week.

Beyond his reputation for surviving punishment, Usubyan has built his entire career on grinding out victories in the toughest of chess matches.

That trait has been a permanent fixture throughout his perfect run on the global stage, and it stretches back even further than that. Fifteen consecutive wins preceded only the second loss of his career in June 2023, a stretch that speaks to a fighter who rarely finds himself outclassed once the gloves are on.

Durability alone does not fully explain that kind of success, though. The 32-year-old pairs his granite chin with sharp timing, quick head movement, an ability to fire off kicks without any telegraphed setup, and a gas tank built to provide fuel deep in a fight without any drop-off in output.

Against a pressure-based athlete like Grigorian, that brand of composure could end up being the deciding factor.

Where lesser opponents tend to wilt the longer the Armenian's relentless volume piles up on them, the Archangel Michael warrior has repeatedly made a habit of settling in and getting stronger the deeper a fight goes.

Outside the technical tools and grit he has shown under the promotional banner, Usubyan carries something extremely dangerous heading into The Inner Circle 25: real ambition for ONE World Title gold.

A win over a fighter of Grigorian's caliber would instantly become the signature victory of his career, and a major step toward his dream of fighting for the ONE Featherweight Kickboxing World Title.

Their quarterfinal clash is the first of four to kick off the ONE SAMURAI Featherweight Kickboxing Tournament across the promotion's stacked triple-header weekend.

The remaining three quarterfinals get underway at ONE SAMURAI 2 inside EBARA WAVE Arena Ota just a day later, where Masaaki Noiri meets Liu "Spirit Dragon" Mengyang, Kaito Ono faces Mohammad Siasarani, and Kosuke "Unstoppable Phoenix" Takagi squares off against Luo Chao. Whoever emerges victorious in this massive tournament will earn a guaranteed shot at reigning divisional king Superbon.

Given what awaits the winner, every warrior will be at their absolute best in this tournament. And that is precisely why overcoming the Armenian would carry so much weight for Usubyan. It would also supply the exact kind of hunger and confidence needed to power through the rest of the bracket.

title: 'Massive club' Cardiff must step up a level, says Pulis
description: Tony Pulis believes Cardiff City is a massive club that would grace the Premier League, but warns they will need to step up a level as they return to the Championship after a season in League One.  The experienced former Premier League manager - whose lengthy career included spells in charge at Stoke City, Crystal Palace, West Bromwich Albion and Middlesbrough - was impressed by the Bluebirds as they won promotion in their first season under boss Brian Barry-Murphy.  "Obviously Cardiff had a fantastic season last year and they get promoted back up to the Championship," Newport-born Pulis told Radio Wales Breakfast.
fullText:
Tony Pulis believes Cardiff City is a massive club that would grace the Premier League, but warns they will need to step up a level as they return to the Championship after a season in League One.

The experienced former Premier League manager - whose lengthy career included spells in charge at Stoke City, Crystal Palace, West Bromwich Albion and Middlesbrough - was impressed by the Bluebirds as they won promotion in their first season under boss Brian Barry-Murphy.

"Obviously Cardiff had a fantastic season last year and they get promoted back up to the Championship," Newport-born Pulis told Radio Wales Breakfast.

"They've got a massive challenge on next year. The Championship is getting stronger and stronger every season.

"You know, for me, Cardiff is a massive football club, always has been in my mind, and would definitely be a great addition to the Premier League, never mind the Championship.

"So it'll be interesting to see what Brian does."

Cardiff, who were runners-up to Lincoln City as they made an immediate bounce-back from League One, have signed Lincoln midfielder Jack Moylan in preparation for their return to the second tier.

The 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international is only the second signing of the summer for Cardiff, who converted goalkeeper Nathan Trott's successful promotion-winning loan spell from Copenhagen into a permanent deal in May.

"I think recruitment is massive and obviously investment. If you've got the investment and the recruitment right, then you've got a chance," added 68-year-old Pulis.

"I think they will need to step up a level. I think Brian's obviously put an identity on the football club, the way they play.

"So things are looking really bright down there at the moment."

The Knights (59-50) got out to a strong start in the doubleheader against Durham (50-58).

In the bottom of the second, Korey Lee doubled with one out, and he advanced to third on a ground out by Tim Elko. That set the stage for Mario Camilletti, who drove in the game's first run with a single. title: 'Kind of surreal.' HOF Fan Fest attracts football lovers and foodies
description: Sugardale Fan Fest was an oasis of football lovers, foodies and those looking for fun. The event kicked off Aug. 5 and continues through Aug. 9.
fullText:
CANTON − Football lovers were hungry and fanatical as Sugardale Fan Fest kicked off at Stadium Park on Aug. 5 during the Pro Football Hall of Fame Enshrinement Festival.

Outrageously attired NFL fans represented their favorite teams. Cheerleaders for the Arizona Cardinals and Carolina Panthers were on hand, both squads in town for the Hall of Fame Game on Aug. 6 at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium. And foodies were in heaven at the new ticketed USA Today Great American Tailgate event.

The Great American Tailgate features 32 food samples representing each of the 32 NFL franchises. Cheesesteaks, street corn, burgers, hot dogs, barbecue pork and mac and cheese were among the tempting eats, often jazzed up beyond the traditional version.

Mark Heise, 60, of Venice, Florida, came to Canton both for the Great American Tailgate and to see Larry Fitzgerald of the Arizona Cardinals be enshrined into the Pro Football Hall of Fame at a ceremony Aug. 8.

His son, Austin Heise, 34, of Venice, Florida, said Fitzgerald is elite.

"He's the best wide receiver of my generation," said the younger Heise.

Coming to the Pro Football Hall of Fame and enshrinement festival for the first time has "been a bucket list thing," he added. "And it's kind of surreal. I'm standing on ground that paved the way for today's game."

Live music and more Jefferson Starship cranks out the classic rock at HOF Fan Fest

Admission is free to Fan Fest, which runs noon to 8 p.m. Aug. 6; noon to 10 p.m. Aug. 7-8; and noon to 8 p.m. Aug. 9. Fan Fest takes place in the main parking lot of Stadium Park along Fulton Road near Stadium Park Drive, about 200 yards below the Pro Football Hall of Fame museum.

title: NFL analysts rip apart Justin Herbert and Madison Beer’s Taylor Swift-Travis Kelce gimmick at Chargers camp
description: Los Angeles Chargers star Justin Herbert’s training camp stunt with Madison Beer gets ruthlessly called out. Just a month or so ago, the NFL’s power couple – Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift – tied the knot at the iconic Madison Square Garden.
fullText:
Los Angeles Chargers star Justin Herbert's training camp stunt with Madison Beer gets ruthlessly called out.

Just a month or so ago, the NFL's power couple – Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift – tied the knot at the iconic Madison Square Garden.

The wedding became a massive talking point for NFL fans and experts alike. Now, it feels like a new power couple has emerged in the league.

It's none other than Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert and American singer Madison Beer.

With the NFL training camp now underway, most head coaches want their players to be entirely focused on football. However, Herbert seems to be distracted by his girlfriend.

After all, a clip of Herbert and Beer sitting together at the Chargers' camp recently went viral. Fans had mixed reactions to it, but NFL analysts Nick Wright and Chris Broussard utterly destroyed the couple's act.

"What is this? Listen, I understand everyone wants to be Travis and Taylor. I get it. I don't blame you. They never did this at the practice field.

"What is happening here? And you know what? I'm not afraid of the Madison Beer fan army, because I got the Swifties on my side and they roll deeper than these folks," Wright said.

He added, "You can't have more videos of your girlfriend fixing your hair than playoff wins when you're in the league for seven years."

Wright's co-host shared the same sentiment as he announced his love for Herbert, but still couldn't defend the Chargers QB's actions.

"This has to be a joke. … You can't let that happen. I'm sorry. I get it, you're in love and all that, but come on! … And I like Justin Herbert, but what! What is this! What in the world is going on?" Broussard said.

The analyst duo understood the feelings of Herbert and Beer, but asked them to keep such interactions private as they want them to follow in the footsteps of Kelce and Swift, who maintained a clear boundary.

title: What strengths might Barcola bring to Anfield?
description: At first glance, Bradley Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz, with the underlying data suggesting the Paris St-Germain forward could fill that void.  Opta's player similarity model rates the Frenchman as the winger whose output most closely resembled Diaz's across Europe's top five leagues in 2025-26 (78%), with Mohamed Salah (65%), Lamine Yamal (61%) and Vinicius Junior (61%) the next closest matches.  Barcola is a left winger by trade, having played almost all of his Champions League minutes for PSG on that flank, but his game is shaped by a centre-forward's instincts.
fullText:
At first glance, Bradley Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz, with the underlying data suggesting the Paris St-Germain forward could fill that void.

Opta's player similarity model rates the Frenchman as the winger whose output most closely resembled Diaz's across Europe's top five leagues in 2025-26 (78%), with Mohamed Salah (65%), Lamine Yamal (61%) and Vinicius Junior (61%) the next closest matches.

A closer look, however, suggests Liverpool would not simply be replacing one winger with another.

Barcola is a left winger by trade, having played almost all of his Champions League minutes for PSG on that flank, but his game is shaped by a centre-forward's instincts. He played as a striker until the age of 17, something reflected in his movement and shot selection.

Last season, he averaged 3.5 shots per 90 minutes in Ligue 1, placing him among the division's most active shooters despite operating from wide areas.

His 9.83 expected goals (xG) ranked in the 95th percentile among wingers across Europe's top five leagues, meaning only around 5% of wide players consistently found themselves in better goalscoring positions.

Barcola converted those chances into 11 league goals, outperforming his xG, while no PSG player or Ligue 1 winger recorded a higher xG total during the 2025-26 campaign.

Those instincts are reflected in how he attacks defenders. Barcola was the only player across Europe's top five leagues to average more than two shot-ending carries per 90 minutes (2.06), illustrating his ability to drive at opponents before creating shooting opportunities for himself.

He also averaged 8.69 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes - the seventh-highest figure among more than 1,500 eligible players - reinforcing the profile of a winger who consistently occupies goalscoring positions.

His shot map highlights a player who attacks dangerous central areas rather than settling for speculative efforts from distance.

The comparison with Salah is equally revealing. While both pose a significant goal threat, Barcola is a more direct ball carrier.

He attempted more take-ons per 90 than the Egypt forward last season (4.26 to 3.38), but created fewer chances (2.16 to 2.33), attempted far fewer crosses (1.15 to 4.89) and through balls (0.25 to 0.59).

The numbers point towards a player who looks to eliminate defenders himself rather than orchestrate attacks from wide areas.

There are also signs that his game continues to evolve under Luis Enrique.

Barcola's passing profile across his three Champions League campaigns at PSG has become increasingly focused on progressing play in the final third, reflecting greater tactical maturity. Rather than dribbling at every opportunity, he now shows a better understanding of when to accelerate attacks and when to recycle possession.

His work without the ball is another reason Liverpool's recruitment team are understood to admire him. Barcola ranked ninth across Europe's top five leagues for possessions won in the final third last season, a metric that reflects the aggressive pressing and intensity likely to be demanded under Andoni Iraola.

title: Kavuma-McQueen and Walsh consider loan moves
description: Chelsea academy duo Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Reggie Walsh consider loan moves away from Stamford Bridge.
fullText:
Chelsea academy duo Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Reggie Walsh are weighing up their loan options away from Stamford Bridge.

The pair are among the star players emerging from Chelsea's Cobham-based training centre and have been part of new manager Xabi Alonso's pre-season tour of Asia and Australia.

However, Portsmouth are plotting to take Kavuma-McQueen, 17, on a season-long loan deal into the Championship after Chelsea's tour and believe they are in pole position.

Furthermore, Walsh, also 17, is exploring his options due to a high-level of competition in Alonso's midfield.

Shim Mheuka, Ishe Samuels-Smith and Omari Kellyman are also available for loan and are likely to move to the Championship, although Kellyman is also considering options overseas.

It follows Genesis Antwi moving to sister club Strasbourg as a host of academy players get impressive loans, notably Jesse Derry joining Portuguese giants Sporting and Harrison Murray-Campbell moving to Belgian top flight side Kortrijk.

There are already seven academy stars on loan away from Stamford Bridge this summer.

title: ‘He will make mistakes…’ – Jamie Carragher has one worry about Andoni Iraola at Liverpool
description: Jamie Carragher has expressed one concern about Andoni Iraola heading into the Basque’s first season as Liverpool head coach.The 44-year-old has replaced Arne Slot in the Anfield dugout, being award...
fullText:
Jamie Carragher has expressed one concern about Andoni Iraola heading into the Basque's first season as Liverpool head coach.

The 44-year-old has replaced Arne Slot in the Anfield dugout, being awarded the job off the back of his excellent work at Bournemouth, who finished just one place and three points behind the Reds last term despite having a far inferior budget.

DOWNLOAD THE OFFICIAL EMPIRE OF THE KOP APP FOR ALL THE LATEST & BREAKING UPDATES – STRAIGHT TO YOUR PHONE! ON APPLE & GOOGLE PLAY

Iraola will embark upon his first Champions League campaign as a coach in a few weeks' time, which brings with it eight midweek fixtures between September and January (plus any knockout phase involvement thereafter) and the challenges of balancing domestic and European commitments.

Speaking to Football Ramble, Carragher raised apprehensions about how the new Liverpool boss handles that balancing act when he's never experienced it before.

The former Reds defender said: "In an ideal world, I would have loved Iraola to have had a couple of European campaigns, won a trophy, been involved in a cup final, but at the moment maybe those managers aren't about.

"He will make mistakes because he's not managed a European campaign. How does he rotate? Does he rotate in the 12:30 game on a Saturday after an away game on the Wednesday? Does he stay with the team? Does he come straight back after a game?

"These are all things I remember as a player that players will complain about to managers and staff, and if you've never really had that before, you're still learning on the job and still learning those little details."

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Iraola has managed in Europe previously, but that was with AEK Larnaca in the Europa League eight years ago, and the scrutiny which comes with coaching Liverpool in the Champions League will be far higher.

The Basque has already spoken about needing a deeper squad to contend with the demands of Premier League and European football this season, and the tight turnarounds between midweek and weekend fixtures will surely have a bearing on team selection and tactics, especially if lengthy air travel is involved.

The 44-year-old is renowned for favouring an intense, high-pressing brand of football, the physical demands of which will be difficult to maintain once the fixture calendar has the Reds playing three matches in seven days.

That will be a new challenge for Iraola, but Liverpool wouldn't have hired him if they didn't believe him capable of handling that effectively. Also, even the most successful managers in the game were once rookies who had to – taking Carragher's phrasing – learn on the job.

We fully trust the LFC boss to handle the dual commitments of domestic and European football with competency and learn from any misjudgements which might occur along the way.

title: 1. FC Magdeburg 2026/27 season preview: Transfers, pre-season, predicted lineup & predictions
description: If 2024/25 was the best campaign in 1. FC Magdeburg's history since the fall of the Berlin Wall, last season can be considered a reality check. Following a rollercoaster time, a strong end to the seas...
fullText:
If 2024/25 was the best campaign in 1. FC Magdeburg's history since the fall of the Berlin Wall, last season can be considered a reality check. Following a rollercoaster time, a strong end to the season extended the club's longest spell at 2. Bundesliga.

Petrik Sander and Pascal Ibold played big roles in Magdeburg's change of fortunes. When Markus Fiedler was relieved of his duties after matchday 8, they were sitting bottom of the standings with only three points. After they replaced him with the unlikely duo as a temporary measure, Magdeburg collected more points (4) in the first two outings.

A strong end to Hinrunde revived their hopes of survival as they earned 10 points from their last four games of 2025. They also started the new year with a big win at Braunschweig before things started to turn difficult once again.

However, Mateusz Żukowski's rise to stardom helped to turn the tables one more time. The Polish striker ended the season with 17 goals in only 21 appearances as he narrowly missed out on finishing top-scorer despite having to wait until matchday 13 for his 2. Bundesliga debut due to an injury.

Five wins from their last seven games put them in a favorable position to avoid the drop on the final matchday as a home defeat to Kaiserslautern didn't ruin the party in the end. Despite spending more than half of the season in the relegation zone, Magdeburg ended the campaign in 14th place.

The 65-year-old Petrik Sander worked with the youth teams of Magdeburg for five years before taking the role initially as an interim coach. With Christian Titz's sensational fifth-placed finish fresh in the memory, the club had to act quicker after the false start under the former Hoffenheim II and Stuttgart II coach Fiedler.

Sander helped Energie Cottbus to a Bundesliga promotion two decades ago, and he finished in a respectable 13th place in his debut top-flight season. However, poor results in subsequent jobs at VfR Aalen and TuS Koblenz denied him another opportunity at this level until he built himself up with Magdeburg.

The former striker last started a season as a head coach in one of the top three divisions back in 2010/11. The twist is that Sander is sharing the burden with Pascal Ibold, who is also listed as head coach on the club's website.

The former RB Leipzig man has also been at the club since 2018 in several roles. While Sander is by far the oldest coach in the division, none of the other 17 clubs have younger bosses than the 36-year-old Ibold. Magdeburg's formula of blending experience with youth saved them last season.

More than incoming transfers, Magdeburg's main focus has been extending the contracts of key players. In particular, against all odds, they managed to tie Żukowski to a deal until 2029. The 24-year-old arrived at the club as a full-back, but his staggering form in front of goal in 2026 had several Bundesliga clubs on alert.

Meanwhile, assist-maker Barış Atik also agreed to commit his future to the club that gave him a second chance when he spent months without a club six years ago. Similarly, the captain Dominik Reimann and center-back Tobias Müller signed new deals weeks before the opening game of the season.

They still had to deal with departures of regular starters from every department, though. Danish Center-back Marcus Mathisen joined relegated St. Pauli, while defensive midfielder Silas Gnaka signed for Belarusian champions Maxline Vitebsk.

However, the biggest miss could be the return of Laurin Ulrich to his parent club Stuttgart. Magdeburg fans are still dreaming of signing the player on a permanent transfer after he only missed one game during his highly productive loan spell.

"Laurin Ulrich is and will remain an issue. There is nothing more to say about it at the moment," said Magdeburg's sporting director Peer Jaekel on the first day of August. The attacking midfielder could be integrated into the first team of Stuttgart after taking his good form into pre-season, but he only has a contract until 2027.

Meanwhile, the vastly-experienced Paul Jaeckel and former Irish youth international Anselmo García MacNulty arrived at Avnet-Arena to replace Mathisen and Jean Hugonet, who was reunited with Titz at Hannover as a free agent.

Elsewhere, ex-Borussia Dortmund II midfielder Tony Reitz will hope to take Gnaka's role, while wingers Emmanuel Iyoha and Moritz-Broni Kwarteng brought plenty of experience at this level.

Former Gladbach midfielder Torben Müsel narrowly missed out on a promotion with RW Essen, but his excellent season saw him return to the 2. Bundesliga for the first time in nine years with a move to Magdeburg. The Blue-Whites also completed the loan signings of South Korean youngsters Do-young Yoon and Chung-hyun Lee.

Magdeburg enjoyed a very successful pre-season as they won each of their first five games before a respectable 1-1 draw with West Ham at Avnet-Arena. Former Stuttgart II and BVB II midfielder Falko Michel canceled Max Kilman's opener with a late equalizer.

In their penultimate fixture, new signings Iyoha and Jackel scored either side of the half-time break for a 2-0 victory over Bundesliga newcomers SC Paderborn.

The goalkeeper Reimann will be the captain for the third season running as Atik and Müller are his deputies. MacNulty played a big part during pre-season, while fellow new signing Iyoha will give the team options with his versatility.

Finnish international Luka Hyryläinen hopes to have more playing time than his debut season. Atik and Żukowski will continue to be the focal points of the attack.

Predicted Lineup (4-3-3): Reimann ©; Iyoha, Müller, MacNulty, Bockhorn; Hyryläinen, Müsel, Michel; Atik, Żukowski, Nollenberger

Magdeburg will start their campaign at home against Eintracht Braunschweig before traveling to newly-promoted VfL Osnabrück. Fifth-tier Bahlinger SC are their opponents in the first round of the DFB-Pokal. The 1974 Cup Winners' Cup winners were eliminated from the domestic cup in the first hurdle in six of the last eight seasons.

Elb-Clásico games against fellow former East German giants Dynamo Dresden will be played on matchday 8 and 25. With their last four games pitting them against Wolfsburg, Nürnberg, Bochum and Heidenheim, it could be very difficult if they once again leave it late.

As mentioned, the new contracts for the key players would go a long way to create stability in Magdeburg. A top-half finish could be plausible, but the main focus will once again be on avoiding a drop to 3. Liga.

title: Lewis-Skelly impressed with Arsenal’s youngsters despite loss to Real Betis

title: La Liga club stand firm on €16 million price tag for Barcelona defensive target
description: Barcelona have not made any defensive reinforcements this summer but have different players on their radar.The Catalan club have been tracking the progress of Racing Santander player Jorge Salinas, bu...
fullText:
Barcelona have not made any defensive reinforcements this summer but have different players on their radar.

The Catalan club have been tracking the progress of Racing Santander player Jorge Salinas, but a move has not transpired so far.

Barça wanted to complete the move before 1 July, insisting that his release clause was €8 million, since Racing had not officially been promoted to La Liga.

However, the newly-promoted club have insisted on the €16 million release clause from the outset, leaving the two clubs apart in negotiations.

Speaking about Salinas' future, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo, Racing sporting director Chema Aragon insisted the versatile defender will only leave if a club triggers his €16 million release clause.

Barcelona remain keen on Salinas. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Barcelona's current valuation is significantly lower, with the Catalan club prepared to offer around €6 million.

Aragon admitted that Racing would struggle to stop one of Europe's biggest clubs if the clause is paid, but stressed that the club's priority is to keep hold of one of their brightest young talents.

"We want our best players to stay," he said, while acknowledging that "there is little you can do if a giant comes along and pays the clause."

Despite the growing transfer speculation, Aragon revealed that Salinas has handled the situation impeccably.

The Racing director described the teenager's attitude as "exemplary", praising the defender for returning to pre-season in excellent condition and never attempting to force a move away from the club.

He also confirmed that Racing are prepared to reward the youngster with an improved contract if he remains beyond the end of the transfer window.

Jorge Salinas' release clause stands at €16 million. (Photo courtesy: Instagram/@jorgesaliiinas)

"If he stays, we'll have to recognize his growth in his contract as well," Aragon explained.

Salinas' ability to operate both as a left-back and a central defender makes him an attractive option for Barcelona, particularly given the club's focus on signing young players with positional versatility.

However, the sizeable gap between Racing's €16 million valuation and Barcelona's reported €6 million offer means there is currently no obvious path to an agreement.

If Barça are that keen to sign the Under-19 Euros champion, they will have to increase their offer significantly for the newly promoted club to consider it.

Salinas is not a priority for Barcelona this summer, but he is a developmental bet who can explode in the future.

It is up to Deco now to figure out how to sweeten the deal and convince Racing to sell Salinas in the coming weeks.

fullText:
On the latest Albion Unlimited podcast, BBC Radio Sussex's Johnny Cantor is joined by former Brighton forward Warren Aspinall as they discuss the Seagulls' possible opponents in the Conference League play-off tie.

Brighton will face CFR Cluj (Romania) or Tromso (Norway) in the key fixture.

Cluj and Tromso are yet to face each other in their two-legged tie, but Cantor believes Tromso could pose a "potential banana skin" for Fabian Hurzeler's side.

"They are placed third in the Norwegian season, which is deep into the campaign as they play across the summer," said Cantor.

In Tromso's Norwegian Eliteserien campaign, they have lost two out of 16 possible games.

In the Romanian SuperLiga, Cluj are also in fourth position, but they have only played three games in the 2026-27 campaign.

Cluj and Tromso's second leg tie will be played on 13 August, with the winner facing Brighton in a two-legged tie on 20 and 27 August, with the Seagulls at home for the second leg.

title: Antonelli opens up about outstanding season so far: 'I didn't expect this'
description: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings heading into the Formula 1 summer break. The Italian has been satisfied with his season so far, but stressed that the job is far from finished.
fullText:
Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings heading into the Formula 1 summer break. The Italian has been satisfied with his season so far, but stressed that the job is far from finished.

The young Italian has impressed so far in the 2026 Formula 1 season. After finishing second behind George Russell in Australia, he won five Grands Prix in a row.

Car issues hampered Antonelli at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya and Silverstone, but he bounced back by winning at Spa-Francorchamps before securing another podium finish at the Hungaroring.

As a result, he holds a 50-point lead over Lewis Hamilton and a 59-point advantage over Russell at the halfway point of the season.

Looking back at the season so far, Antonelli said: "Well, for sure, I did not expect to find myself in this position. But, you know, the car has been extremely good, the team has done an incredible job and, on my side, I try to maximize every opportunity I have."

The Mercedes driver added: "Of course, there's still lots of work to do, lots to learn, but it was a good first half of the season. Now I'm looking forward to the second half and we're just going to keep pushing."

Despite his lead in the standings, former Formula 1 driver Gerhard Berger is not ready to back Antonelli over Russell in the title fight, pointing to last season as proof that the championship can quickly swing after Oscar Piastri appeared to be the clear favorite midway through the year.

He said to F1.com: "I don't think it's the right way to put money on it (who becomes world champion). One is the risky, young, hot blood, the other is already much more experienced and will play the ball back into Antonelli's field. Last year, in the beginning, it looked like Oscar Piastri was going to beat Lando Norris, and Norris turned the page around and won the championship. That's all open in F1. It will be open until the end."

title: How could Newcastle play under Jaissle?
description: Matthias Jaissle's predecessor Eddie Howe had similar principles in terms of building a side around physical intensity, pressing and direct attacks.  Howe's defensive tactics should align well with the Red Bull Salzburg style of pressing, which could make it easier for the players to buy into Jaissle's methods.  What Howe was criticised for towards the end of his tenure, though, was a supposed lack of adaptability.
fullText:
Matthias Jaissle's predecessor Eddie Howe had similar principles in terms of building a side around physical intensity, pressing and direct attacks.

The German primarily uses a high-pressing 4-4-2 when the opposition are building from the back.

Even when his teams are pushed into more of a mid-block, they have shown an impressive understanding of when to step forward and transition into a high press as a collective.

Howe's defensive tactics should align well with the Red Bull Salzburg style of pressing, which could make it easier for the players to buy into Jaissle's methods.

What Howe was criticised for towards the end of his tenure, though, was a supposed lack of adaptability.

After joining Al-Ahli, Jaissle inherited a mosaic of superstars and less experienced Saudi players - a wildly different challenge from coaching a Red Bull club with consistency and understanding in style from youth level through to first team.

While he retained his coaching principles, he recognised the need to platform players according to their individual strengths within that framework.

The Premier League is constantly evolving, with coaches designing new counter-measures to tactics that appear to work from one week to the next.

If Jaissle is going to succeed in the English top flight, that agility will be a vital asset.

title: Check out the Johannesburg-Lewiston high school football schedule
description: Johannesburg-Lewiston football hopes to find success in a new-look Northern Michigan Football Conference; take a look at their 2026 schedule breakdown.
fullText:
JOHANNESBURG ― We're on team three of three of our Gaylord area high school football schedule breakdowns. Next week, teams will be back on the field for the first official practices of the 2026 season. We've covered what Gaylord and Gaylord St. Mary are looking forward to this year ― now it's Johannesburg-Lewiston's turn.

It would've been hard to predict the past five years of JoBurg football when they left the Thirbly Field in Traverse City on Jan. 16, 2021 after the Division 8 state semifinals. One of Northern Michigan's most consistent programs in the 2010s is now 5-38 in the last five seasons. With a new-look conference yet a familiar-looking schedule, will this be the year JoBurg returns to its winning ways?

St. Mary GSM football enters new conference, faces new look schedule in 2026

GHS Gaylord High School football schedule breakdown, 2026

Last matchup: Tawas 21, JoBurg 6 (Sept. 13, 2024)

A few more teams left the Northern Michigan Football Conference this offseason, prompting the league to officially ditch the divisions and reformat as a nine-team conference with an eight-game schedule. That makes this game, formerly a cross-divisional battle, a season opener and league opener for both teams.

Tawas and JL both finished 1-8 last year, making this a key battle for both teams to gauge their progress.

It's somewhat hard to believe these two programs have never crossed paths on the football field, but it will now be an annual event in the NMFC as JL heads to Bezonia in Week 2. Benzie Central went 2-7 in 2026 but had solid offensive showings against Tawas (56-0) and Oscoda (54-12).

Sept. 11 vs. Oscoda (Military Appreciation Night)

Last matchup: JoBurg 26, Oscoda 14 (Oct. 3, 2025)

JL got its lone win of the 2025 season at Oscoda in Week 6 last year. Now, they host the Owls in Week 3, a chance for the Cardinals to pick up a league victory in the new-look NMFC.

Last matchup: Frankfort 41, JoBurg 30 (Sept. 12, 2025)

The game against Frankfort may have been JL's best showing in 2025, losing by just 11 points to a future playoff team. Where JL stands after Week 4 will say a lot about this team's progression, so use this as a measuring stick matchup in about a month.

Sept. 25 at Maple City Glen Lake

Last matchup: Glen Lake 49, JoBurg 6 (Oct. 10, 2025)

Maple City Glen Lake won the final NMFC-Legacy Championship and a Division 8 district championship in 2025. Now, they enter the new NMFC as a top contender to win another league title.

Last matchup: Mancelona 44, JoBurg 6 (Oct. 17, 2025)

The wheels had fallen off for JL by the time the Ironmen came to town, but Mancy showed just how big the gap was between the Cardinals and the top half of the league when they rolled through JoBurg late last season.

Last matchup: EJ 51, JoBurg 0 (Sept. 5, 2025)

This Week 2 shutout was a disappointment for JL's coaches after a solid performance against Burton Bendle in Week 1. Now, JL will have more than a few weeks to prepare for a team that owns a five-game win streak over the Cardinals, but will need to bring a healthy team to EJ for a chance at an upset victory.

Last matchup: Harbor 45, JoBurg 12 (Sept. 19, 2025)

Despite the struggles of the last five years, JL could usually count on at least one league win when they played Harbor Springs. That changed in 2025, leaving the Cardinals without a league win for the first time since 2021.

The league finale for JL, this is a major final test for how far the JLHS program has progressed.

Last matchup: Manton 50, JoBurg 8 (Oct. 24, 2025)

JL and Manton have met in Week 9 each of the last five seasons: different matchup, same story for JL. The Rangers have won five straight over the Cardinals, last year's 42-point victory being the most lopsided of the five matchups. JoBurg's lone non-conference gam, this matchup featured a playoff team last year; JoBurg hopes it will feature two this season.
