title: Cyclospora has expanded to fruit, other vegetables: Ex-CDC director
description: Redfield advised caution should be exercised with consuming raw vegetables beyond bagged lettuce.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — As the cyclospora outbreak continues to expand around the country, Dr. Robert Redfield is urging people to stay away from certain fruits and vegetables beyond lettuce.

The CDC reports that an additional six states are reporting cases of cyclosporiasis, with over 22,000 cases confirmed or suspected overall in the U.S.

Michigan, which reported the first two deaths from the outbreak, has become a hotspot for the parasite, with more than 11,000 confirmed cases. Officials confirmed both individuals who died had significant underlying health conditions.

Beyond that, health officials in the U.K. have said they've witnessed a substantial increase in cases among travelers returning from Mexico. Investigators have linked some cases to lettuce grown in Mexico and distributed by Taylor Farms, though the outbreak's full source has not been confirmed.

Redfield, a former CDC director, told "Elizabeth Vargas Reports" that the parasite has also been found in blueberries, raspberries and snow peas.

"You have to get those vegetables that were contaminated with human fecal material. And so it's not something we see a lot in the United States," he said.

The doctor stated that caution should be exercised when consuming raw vegetables beyond bagged lettuce.

"The safest thing to do is get locally grown vegetables because the real risk is these internationally imported vegetables right now," Redfield noted. "The only way you get cyclosporiasis is if you have to eat vegetables."

Expanding on the vegetables, Redfield pointed out the parasite is "very hard to wash off."

"So if you wash your lettuce and you put it in a lettuce spinner and you have cyclospora in that lettuce, it's still going to be there," he said. "You can't wash it off."

Redfield acknowledged the sickness is treatable for those who get ill for more than 48 hours.

"It's actually susceptible to an antibiotic we call Septra or Bactrim," he explained. "So rather than take two to four weeks to get better, you might get better in five to seven days."

NewsNation's Alex Caprariello contributed to this report.

title: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong warns of new military options over Japan's strike capabilities
description: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, warned on Wednesday that Pyongyang would adopt "additional military
fullText:
SEOUL, Aug 5 (Reuters) - North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, warned on Wednesday that Pyongyang would adopt "additional ‌military options" in response to what she called Japan's transformation into a military power, ‌after Tokyo test-fired a U.S.-made Tomahawk cruise missile.

In a statement carried by state media KCNA, Kim accused Japan of moving beyond ​a defensive posture and turning its armed forces into a force capable of pre-emptive attacks and overseas military operations.

She cited Japan's recent Tomahawk test from the Aegis destroyer Chokai in the Pacific Ocean, as well as test-firings of other missiles and its participation in a U.S.-led joint military drill in the Philippines in ‌May.

Kim said that North Korea would ⁠respond in ways that made Japan feel that its security has been exposed to greater danger. "We should make it regret," she said, in some of her ⁠strongest rhetoric toward Tokyo in recent months.

Kim also accused the United States of enabling Japan's military buildup by supplying Tomahawk missiles, modifying vessels for their operation and supporting the missile tests.

"The U.S. is behind such dangerous ​military moves ​of Japan," she said.

Kim, who heads the record-keeping department ​in North Korea's ruling party, said Japan's ‌acquisition of long-range strike capabilities effectively placed North Korea and other neighbouring countries within range.

To counter Tokyo's military activities that may pose a potential threat to the security of North Korea, Kim said Pyongyang "will set up additional military options," without elaborating.

The statement is the latest in a series of North Korean commentaries criticising security cooperation among the United States, South Korea and Japan.

Since July, KCNA has published at ‌least six editorials and commentaries denouncing these joint military ​activities as threatening regional security and raising tensions on the ​Korean Peninsula.

Analysts said Pyongyang is seeking to ​portray Japan's military modernisation as a direct security threat to justify its own ‌weapons development.

Yang Moo-jin, a professor at the University ​of North Korean Studies ​in Seoul, said Kim's comments attempt to frame Tokyo's steps as part of a broader U.S. effort to strengthen its proxy military capabilities to counter North Korea.

The messaging could lay the ​groundwork for possible future military demonstrations, ‌including missile tests or displays of undersea strike capabilities, said Lim Eul-chul, a professor ​at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies.

title: Bill aiming for peace between Turkey and Kurdish fighters goes to parliament
description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling party on Wednesday filed a bill in parliament to advance a peace initiative aimed at ending the decades‑long conflict with Kurdish militants, including ...
fullText:
ANKARA, Turkey (AP) — Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling party on Wednesday filed a bill in parliament to advance a peace initiative aimed at ending the decades‑long conflict with Kurdish militants, including a provision for an effective pardon for former fighters.

The Kurdistan Workers' Party, or PKK, last year declared its decision to disarm and disband as part of the peace effort with Turkey, following a call by its imprisoned leader, Abdullah Ocalan. The PKK then staged a symbolic disarmament ceremony in northern Iraq, where it is based, and announced that it was withdrawing fighters from key locations in Turkey to Iraq.

The bill toward "strengthening national solidarity and social cohesion" defines the procedures for overseeing the PKK's disarmament and the judicial treatment of its members.

Parliament's Justice Committee on Friday will consider the bill before a debate in the general assembly, said Abdullah Guler, chair of the Justice and Development Party's parliamentary group. The government hopes it passes before the summer recess later this month.

"The critical threshold is the surrender, disarmament and destruction of the PKK terrorist organization's weapons and the establishment of a mechanism to determine this process," he told a news conference.

The proposal was submitted with the support of 360 parliamentary deputies, Guler said, with more expected to sign up in the coming days.

The PKK still has the bulk of its arsenal. A decommissioning mechanism will rely on confirmation by the National Security Council that the group has been disbanded and its weapons surrendered.

The rehabilitation of PKK members is expected to include a pardon for about 4,000 members not directly involved in violence once the group is dissolved. This could pave the way for the release of people convicted of crimes such as PKK membership or supporting the group financially or through propaganda.

It will also allow the return of PKK members based in Syria and Iraq or in exile in European countries, Hurriyet newspaper reported.

Ongoing investigations and prosecutions for such crimes would be postponed for a period dependent on the severity of the alleged offenses, Guler said. If no terror-related crime is committed within the time frame, the case will be dropped.

Applications to benefit from the law must be made within six months of its publication in the Official Gazette, Guler said. A ministerial committee and a parliamentary commission will monitor the process.

Militants convicted of intentional homicide and those sentenced to life sentences before 2005 are excluded from the bill's provisions. This applies to Ocalan and other senior PKK figures.

The pro-Kurdish DEM Party has lobbied for Ocalan, who has been imprisoned since 1999, to be granted official status to coordinate the transition process, leading to his release. Although this is not in the current proposal, media reports suggest it may be considered later.

Instead, Ocalan's situation in his island prison likely will be improved, giving him broader visiting conditions and communication with the outside world.

Turkey's peace process with the PKK is already impacting the region, allowing an oil agreement and trade ties with Iraq and helping Syria to integrate areas that were held by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, said Hamish Kinnear, Middle East and North Africa analyst at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft.

"The PKK ceasefire, alongside the crisis in the Persian Gulf, has facilitated Iraq-Turkey trade ties, with both powers recently signing a deal for the flow of oil through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline," Kinnear said in a note.

"Further progress for the Turkey-PKK peace process will also facilitate the efforts of the Syrian government to integrate areas of the country formerly held by the Syrian Democratic Forces," he said in reference to the group, which has links to the PKK.

The PKK has waged an armed insurgency since 1984, which has claimed tens of thousands of lives and spilled into Iraq and Syria. It has been designated a terrorist organization by Turkey, the United States and the European Union.

The group initially sought an independent Kurdish state but later shifted to demands for autonomy and expanded rights in Turkey. Previous peace efforts between Turkey and the PKK have ended in failure, most recently in 2015.

The proposed law is intended as a temporary legal framework that could last up to four years, although parliament could extend the period. It is anticipated that further legislation could be introduced to tackle other issues such as Ocalan's release.

In a message conveyed through DEM Party legislators who visited him on Monday, Ocalan announced support for the legislation, saying that "with this law, we are setting out to resolve a historical issue. We are at the beginning of a democratization process that will be at least as significant as the founding of the republic."

title: Soccer-FIFA apologises to members as Infantino holds crisis meeting amid stake sale fallout
description: FIFA said on Wednesday it had apologised to its member associations for mistakes made over its abandoned proposal to sell commercial rights linked to the World Cup, as
fullText:
Aug 5 (Reuters) - FIFA said on Wednesday it had apologised to its member associations for mistakes made over its abandoned proposal to sell commercial rights linked to the World Cup, as the governing body's leadership reaffirmed its support for president Gianni Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco.

Following the meeting in Rabat, attended by Infantino, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and members of FIFA's management board, FIFA said its leadership had reaffirmed its full ‌support for the president while acknowledging that the handling of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal should have been different.

In a statement, FIFA said a separate letter had been sent to FIFA Council members and the 211 member associations apologising ‌for the errors and promising a review.

It added that, with the proposal withdrawn, FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process" and would take all necessary measures to protect its reputation.

Vehicles believed to be carrying Infantino and Grafstrom were seen leaving FIFA's Africa office in Sale after the meeting, which ​came amid mounting criticism of Infantino's leadership ahead of next year's presidential election.

The meeting followed last week's withdrawal of a proposal to sell a 20% stake in a new commercial rights entity to private investors in a deal that would have raised about $4.2 billion for football development.

The proposal, which also drew scrutiny because of the involvement of a company with family links to U.S. President Donald Trump, prompted fierce criticism from European soccer's governing body UEFA and other stakeholders, who accused FIFA of poor governance and a lack of consultation.

The apology underscored FIFA's acknowledgement that mistakes had been made in the handling of his proposal for a new commercial rights body, which has become the most serious challenge to his leadership since he became FIFA president in 2016 after triggering a torrent of criticism from UEFA, several member associations and senior FIFA officials over governance ‌and consultation.

His backdown last Friday has done little to assuage those critics, most notably UEFA, ⁠which accused him of selling the soul of the game and has said it no longer has confidence in his leadership.

That has cast a shadow over Infantino's re-election for a fourth term at the FIFA Congress in Morocco in March, which had looked like a foregone conclusion two months ago.

A handful of European federations have withdrawn their backing for the Swiss Italian, but perhaps more damaging are the messages coming from ⁠Infantino's FIFA colleagues.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also questioned Infantino's leadership on Wednesday, saying he has lost confidence in the FIFA president after learning senior advisers had not been consulted on the abandoned proposal.

"I don't have confidence in Mr. Infantino," Carney told reporters, adding that failing to inform senior executives and fellow board members of such a significant proposal "should be fatal" for any leader.

Grafstrom had sent an internal memo to staff lamenting the "sad and reproachable series of events" that led to the project being "permanently abandoned", two sources told Reuters.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission ​and ​its responsibility towards world football continue," the Swede added in the letter, which made no mention of Infantino by name.

His words echoed those of FIFA's Chief ​Operating Officer Kevin Lamour, who said last week that staff had been "deceived" over the plan which he ‌described as the project of one person.

Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned in protest at the plan last week. Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of Global Football Development, said he had not been involved in drafting the proposal, and called the decision to withdraw it "absolutely necessary".

Former Portugal great Luis Figo, who had planned to run for the FIFA presidency in 2015, said Infantino should resign over the affair, while UEFA Vice-President Laura McAllister told Reuters the controversy surrounding the abandoned proposal had brought the FIFA president's leadership to a crisis point.

Infantino has spent the past week in Morocco, which will co-host the World Cup in 2030 and whose football association has announced its continued support for him.

The meeting was widely seen as an effort to reinforce support for Infantino and ensure that he emerges from the crisis with enough backing to remain the favourite for re-election in March.

An Extraordinary Congress could be called if 43 or more FIFA member associations make a formal written request for one.

Qatar, which hosted the 2022 World Cup, Kuwait, Lebanon, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and the Philippines have declared ‌their loyalty to Infantino.

Infantino has always enjoyed a lot of support away from the traditional heartlands of the game, where impoverished football associations rely on ​FIFA's largesse to operate.

But European Leagues, which represents more than 1,300 clubs across Europe, said FIFA must not be allowed to "continue taking unilaterally disruptive decisions" that affect ​clubs, players and fans. It also criticised the "impractically short assessment timeline" of four weeks given by FIFA to study the plan ​to expand the World Cup from 48 to 64 teams for the 2030 edition.

AFRICAN ADMINISTRATORS BACK INFANTINO

Leading African football administrators have sent messages of support as Infantino looks to the continent's 54 members for backing. The ‌African confederation (CAF) has yet to take a stance.

The executive committee of the smallest and least wealthy ​regional confederation, Oceania, will meet next Wednesday to discuss their approach.

Under FIFA ​rules, the vote of San Marino, whose men's team are ranked 211th and last in the world rankings, counts as much as that of World Cup winners like Brazil, Germany, Argentina and Spain.

One clear advantage for Infantino as he looks to extend his presidency until 2031 is that no clear candidate to stand against him in March's election has yet emerged.

Jordan FA President Prince Ali bin Hussein has twice stood for the post, and he made his position clear on Tuesday when he ​accused FIFA of "blackmail", saying it had offered to help solve problems in exchange for endorsing Infantino.

"We ‌did not endorse him before and certainly will not now," Prince Ali wrote on social media.

A FIFA spokesperson rejected reports that Infantino had made promises over the host of the 2030 World Cup final.

"It is false and misleading to ​claim the FIFA president has made any promise in relation to hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030 Final. A decision will be made by FIFA in due course," the spokesperson said.

title: Olympic champion curler Muirhead comes out of retirement
description: Winter Olympic gold medallist Eve Muirhead revokes her retirement, saying being Team GB's chef de mission at this year's Games has inspired her to return to curling after four years away.
fullText:
Winter Olympic gold medallist Eve Muirhead has reversed her retirement, saying being Team GB's chef de mission at this year's Games has inspired her to return to curling after four years away.

The 36-year-old will team up with two-time Olympic silver medallist Bobby Lammie in mixed doubles this season - the pair having won the world title in 2022 - with a view to ultimately reaching the Alpes 2030 Games.

Four-time Olympian Muirhead stepped away from competing after winning gold in Beijing four years ago, and subsequently spoke about the mental health challenges she experienced towards the end of a 15-year struggle to win gold.

The Scot was Team GB's chef de mission at the Milan-Cortina Games in February and says that "brought back emotions that I had not felt for a long time".

Muirhead explained that being away from curling gave her the chance to try new things, take on new physical challenges, and enjoy the sport "without the pressure I had placed on myself for so many years".

Olympic champion Muirhead retires from curling

How Team GB is leading the way in curling's arms race

"But the competitive side of me never disappeared," she added. "The more time I spent around elite sport and curling, the more I began to wonder whether I still had something to give on the ice.

"I know how demanding the road to an Olympics is, but I am returning from a very different place. I feel refreshed, physically strong and excited by the challenge. I would not be coming back unless I believed I could perform at that level again."

Muirhead's gold medal-winning team-mate Vicky Drummond is also returning to the sport to rival her - and a third member of that rink, Jen Dodds - in the GB Curling mixed doubles programme.

Drummond, 32, says being part of the BBC Sport team in Cortina in February rekindled her passion for competing, and that she wants to show her young daughter Sophie that "becoming a mum doesn't mean your ambitions have to end".

"More than anything, I want my return to mean something beyond the ice," said the intensive care nurse, who will partner Euan Kyle.

"I want Sophie to grow up knowing that it's never too late to chase something that excites you. If she grows up believing that anything is possible because she watched me try, then this journey will already have been worth it.

"I have no idea where this road will lead, but I'm excited to find out."

Spending time with Muirhead and Drummond in Cortina earlier this year, it was clear how much both revelled being back in the elite sport environment and how much curling meant to them.

In Muirhead's case, there was always going to be a void after the all-consuming job of chef de mission ended abruptedly when the Games did.

And her near-zealous completion of Hyrox events around the world - and at a predictably elite level - spoke to the competitive fire still inside her.

At 36, she is still young and will return revived - and with the cachet of having not just won Olympic gold - but dealt with the stresses and strains of that journey. And she will do so with arguably the best sweeper in the sport alongside her.

Drummond is even younger and returns with a different motivation. That is not to say she'll not be just as competitive as her close friend.

The battle between them, and Dodds, to be part of GB's pre-eminent pairing as we move towards the next Winter Olympics will be fascinating.

title: Mourinho, Ferguson & search for new club - what next for Smalling?
description: Snubbing university, genetics testing for supplements, Sir Alex Ferguson and Jose Mourinho - Chris Smalling is not your ordinary footballer.
fullText:
It is clear from the first answer of a fascinating 45-minute chat that Chris Smalling is no ordinary footballer.

A career that took the 36-year-old from non-league Maidstone to a Champions League final in the space of three years, has, so far, led to 580 club appearances in three countries, playing the majority for Sir Alex Ferguson or Jose Mourinho, plus 31 England caps and trophies with Manchester United and Roma.

It has now brought Smalling and his family back to the north west of England to figure out his next steps.

Smalling has plans for his career after playing but presently, he is focused on finding a new club.

"I know my body now better than when I was 26 and that's shown in the games I'm playing," he said.

"When I was younger, I remember Sir Alex was implementing certain things, like Ryan Giggs doing yoga.

"When you get beyond 30, each year is precious in terms of enjoying playing and being passionate about football.

"Actual training is a very short time. The longevity and recovery starts very early in terms of what I'm eating and doing between sessions, even down to my supplements now.

"In pre-season we have blood tests and the clubs make recommendations. I went one step further and kind of had genetics testing, which goes deep into everything. A lot of my supplements were changed because of that."

Smalling was an ever-present for Al-Fayha in the Saudi Pro-League last season, something he is particularly proud of.

His career is not over. Yet wind back 18 years and Smalling did not imagine he was destined to come anywhere near as far as he has.

"It wasn't even plan D," he recalled.

"I was playing at Maidstone, but I was going to university to study financial economics.

"I had everything set out. I already had my A levels, and I was looking at other non-league clubs near Leicester because I still wanted to play.

"It was very late in the summer when the opportunity came around. I knew it was a slim chance even to be offered but I needed to do everything I could."

The offer was from Fulham. Roy Hodgson watched one practice game, called Smalling into his office and offered a contract.

"It wasn't even a full week," said Smalling. "I didn't have any time to get my head around it. I was just in total shock."

It wouldn't be the last time Hodgson put Smalling into a position where he had no time to think.

He was part of the Fulham squad that travelled to Blackburn for a Premier League game on 17 January, 2010. As it turned out, the then 20-year-old would play no part in the 2-0 defeat.

For him, the important part of the trip took place the previous evening.

"There had been a lot of talk about other clubs but not Manchester United," he said.

"Roy pulled me off the coach, said Fulham had accepted a bid and Sir Alex was coming to the hotel in 45 minutes. I called my mum first but then I was sitting in the room thinking it was going to be a bit awkward and what questions could I can ask him?

"Literally, we were there for about at least a couple of hours. He was so calming and reassuring.

"Even I was doubting it because they had all these great centre-backs. I wanted to develop and wondered 'how do I fit in?'.

"He told me I would get a chance and he believed in me.

"To be able to share the dressing room and the pitch and have conversations with him, is just incredible."

It is that personal side which Smalling feels sets the great managers apart.

To outsiders, his relationship with Mourinho is characterised by a public criticism from the Portuguese in November 2016 around an unwillingness to play through an injury.

That is not how Smalling views it.

"For United or Roma, Jose picked me for most games because we had a good relationship and he trusted me.

"It's very easy to influence younger players but the beauty of Sir Alex and Jose is that they were able to create that belief in senior players. A lot of managers can give good team talks but if you look at some eye-to-eye, see the passion and real belief that 'it's going to happen' senior players follow and the rest lock in. That's the beauty of top-class manager.

"In that situation, I was having injections in broken toe because he had created that mentality in me that I could do anything, even if, maybe, I shouldn't. I had reached the limit of the amount [of injections] I could have, had to stop in a warm-up and he was disappointed.

"It gave me even more belief because it was easy to choose another centre-back but he wanted me."

Smalling remains in contact with Mourinho and wished him good luck when he took over at Real Madrid this summer.

He has no plans to follow his old boss into coaching.

"I don't think it will be my route," he said. "I'm quite comfortable with the next stage.

"I'm working on an education programme for young players partnering with the Global Institute of Sport that's going to be coming out shortly. I've got three or four of these types of projects.

"Once my football career comes to an end, I can put more time to them but at the minute it's all focused on playing because I have that passion and drive and physically my stats are good."

Whoever signs Smalling will get more than just a player.

He had a positive input in Al-Fayha's off-field development, ensuring the gym was suitable for the standards an elite modern-day player demands.

He is proud that at all his previous clubs he is remembered fondly and made a positive impact on and off the pitch.

Turning down that university offer was a good move.

"It would have been the safer route," he said.

"In that first year, I was not earning a lot of money. I was playing for the reserves and the 19th man for the first team, travelling around but not quite on the bench. There was no guarantee I was going to earn more money.

"When I signed for United, it was a four-year contract. At the end of the first year, I signed a new one, another a year later and another 18 months after that.

"There was always this carrot. I never took anything for granted."

What happens next with Rashford and Man Utd?

Man Utd admit ticket touting investigation error

title: Players who turned World Cup heroics into big transfers
description: BBC Sport looks back at some of the players whose standout performances at the World Cup earned a big transfer.
fullText:
The World Cup is football's biggest stage, filled with goals, drama and unforgettable moments - but it can also prove to be the ultimate shop window.

World Cup heroics have transformed players' lives in the past, and Vozinha's recent move to Chilean side Colo-Colo after an impressive tournament with Cape Verde is the latest reminder that the competition still has the power to change careers.

At the age of 40, the goalkeeper's journey from the Portuguese second division to Chile's biggest club may be unique, but he is not the first to get a big move after starring on the global stage.

Here are some of the players whose standout performances at the World Cup earned them a big move.

Similar to Vozinha, Marc-Vivien Foe was an unknown name before the 1994 World Cup.

Despite Cameroon's disappointing World Cup campaign in the USA, compared to their historic run in 1990, Foe emerged as one of the team's best performers during his debut tournament.

A standout game against Brazil caught attention, which then led to a free transfer from Cameroon's Canon Yaounde to French side Lens.

Foe spent four years at Lens and helped them achieve their first league title in the 1997-98 season.

He also played for West Ham United, Manchester City and Lyon, where he won the French League Cup and Lyon's first Ligue 1 title in 2002.

Foe tragically passed away in June 2003 after he collapsed during a Confederations Cup semi-final against Colombia.

Gilberto Silva's first appearance at a World Cup came in 2002, when the tournament was hosted in South Korea and Japan.

The 25-year-old, who played in Brazil's top division for Atletico Miniero, returned home as a World Cup winner who played every minute of every game for Luiz Felipe Scolari's team.

Silva was only brought into the starting XI because Brazil captain Emerson was ruled out by injury.

But, after playing a key role in Brazil's triumph, the midfielder earned a move to Premier League champions Arsenal.

Nicknamed 'The Invisible Wall', the defensive midfielder joined the Gunners from Atletico Mineiro for about £4.5m.

During his six years in north London, Silva won two FA Cups and played a key role in the famous 2003-04 Invincibles side that went unbeaten to claim the Premier League title.

At the age of 22, Javier Mascherano announced himself on the global stage at the 2006 World Cup, where he helped Argentina reach the quarter-finals.

His performances for both his club back in Brazil and at the World Cup drew the attention of European clubs.

Mascherano initially expressed his desire to remain at Corinthians and help the club in their relegation battle.

However, he soon made the move to West Ham United in the summer of 2006 alongside his Argentina team-mate Carlos Tevez, who also impressed at the World Cup in Germany.

Mascherano had a brief spell with the Hammers until the beginning of 2007, leaving to join Liverpool where he featured in their 2007 Champions League final defeat by AC Milan.

Mascherano then played for Barcelona from 2010, winning the Champions League twice and being part of squads that won La Liga on five occasions.

At the age of just 21, Mesut Ozil emerged as one of the world's most exciting young players after he helped Germany finish third at the 2010 World Cup.

After registering four goals and four assists in seven games, Ozil was able to show off his quality and prove he was a standout performer.

Big clubs took note, and by August 2010, Ozil switched Werder Bremen for Real Madrid, for a fee of about 15m euros (£12.4m).

Copa del Rey, La Liga and Spanish Super Cup titles were to follow during his three year stay in Madrid, before becoming Arsenal's record signing for £42.4m in 2013.

James Rodriguez became one of the stars of the 2014 World Cup, scoring six goals for Colombia and winning the Golden Boot after a memorable run to the quarter-finals.

His excellent performances, including his famous volley against Uruguay, earned him a spot in Fifa's team of the tournament.

The volley against Uruguay was later voted as the best goal in the tournament by more than four million people on Fifa's website and won the Fifa Puskas Award for the best goal of the year.

Real Madrid decided to sign Rodriguez from Monaco for about 75m euros (£71m) after the tournament - a move that led to him winning multiple trophies with Los Blancos, including two Champions Leagues.

Well, you knew this one was coming.

Vozinha became a cult hero when Cape Verde claimed their first World Cup point against Spain in the group stage and his social media fame has exploded from 50,000 Instagram followers to nearly 30 million.

After helping his team reach the knockout stages, taking finalists Argentina to extra time in the last 32, Vozinha was named in Fifa's team of the tournament and even had a newly discovered species of sea slug named after him.

Vozinha's career has taken him to Slovakia, Angola, Moldova, Cyprus and, until recently, Portuguese second division side Chaves, but he has always believed himself to be a "big club player".

Joining Colo Colo, the most successful team in the Primera Division (34 titles) and Copa Chile (14), is his career "highlight".

Gheorghe Hagi - Brescia to Barcelona (1994)

Dejan Stankovic - Red Star Belgrade to Lazio (1998)

Carlos Salcido - Guadalajara to PSV Eindhoven (2006)

Nicolas Otamendi - Velez Sarsfield to Porto (2010)

Edinson Cavani - Palermo to Napoli (2010)

Sami Khedira - Stuttgart to Real Madrid (2010)

Alexis Sanchez - Udinese to Barcelona (2010)

Keylor Navas - Levante to Real Madrid (2014)

Enner Valencia - Pachuca to West Ham United (2014)

Enzo Fernandez - Benfica to Chelsea (2022)

Vozinha to join Chilean club after World Cup heroics

Vozinha granted shirt name exemption by Chile FA

title: A wanted man - but would Liverpool's Gakpo be a good fit at Spurs?
description: The data behind Tottenham's interest in Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo and how he could fit into Roberto de Zerbi’s side.
fullText:
Tottenham are keen on a move for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo as Roberto de Zerbi continues reshaping his squad.

Any deal would be far from straightforward. Liverpool are reluctant to weaken their attacking options, particularly after Mohamed Salah's departure and with Hugo Ekitike still recovering from an Achilles injury.

The Reds are themselves pursuing Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola but, even if he arrived, Liverpool would be losing one of their most experienced attackers.

So why are Spurs interested? And what do the numbers suggest Gakpo would bring to De Zerbi's side?

On the surface, Gakpo looks like another left winger. In reality, he offers considerably more tactical flexibility.

Although he has played most of his football for Liverpool from the left, the Netherlands international has regularly been used as a central striker, false nine and second forward. De Zerbi reportedly views him as someone capable of operating through the middle, dropping between the lines to link play before releasing runners beyond him.

That profile fits the Italian's football. Instead of relying on a traditional penalty-box striker, De Zerbi often asks his centre forward to vacate central spaces, combine with midfielders and create room for wide players to attack. Gakpo possesses the technical quality, close control and positional intelligence to perform that role while also providing cover on the left.

His versatility would also offer Tottenham valuable insurance across multiple positions. Dominic Solanke and Mathys Tel are both natural central forwards, but neither provide the same ability to move seamlessly between the wing and the middle.

Gakpo's 2025-26 campaign divided opinion among Liverpool supporters, with seven Premier League goals representing his lowest return in a full season at Anfield.

The underlying data, however, paints a far more encouraging picture. Though Liverpool struggled collectively, Gakpo actually remained one of Europe's most dangerous wide forwards in terms of finding scoring opportunities. Only seven wingers across Europe's top five leagues averaged more touches in the opposition penalty area than his 2.2 per 90 minutes, while he also ranked inside the top 10 for both open-play shots and chances created.

His player comparison profile reinforces those strengths. Compared with positional peers across Europe's top five leagues, Gakpo ranked in the 98th percentile for shot frequency, the 96th percentile for advanced involvement and the 91st percentile for box threat. In other words, very few wide players became involved in dangerous attacking situations more regularly.

Those numbers are driven by his willingness to attack space behind defences. Gakpo was caught offside 30 times in the Premier League last season, more than any other player, illustrating how often he looked to run beyond the last defender in search of goalscoring opportunities, as opposed to simply receiving the ball to feet.

At his best, Gakpo regularly attacks the back post, times his runs into the penalty area intelligently and arrives centrally despite starting from the left flank. And, while he endured a difficult season last term, he scored regularly for Liverpool as the Reds won the title in 2024-25, with 18 goals in all competitions.

The comparison with Tottenham's existing attackers helps explain the interest.

Gakpo finished last season with a higher expected-goals total (8.59), more shots (87), more assists (five) and more big chances created (10) than any of Spurs' forward options, despite playing in a Liverpool side whose Premier League title defence ended with a fifth-place finish.

Richarlison scored more league goals, but attempted 26 fewer shots and created only half as many big chances. Solanke, limited by injury, produced just 20 shots and one big chance created, while Tel also fell short across several of the key attacking measures. Randal Kolo Muani, who spent last season on loan at Spurs before joining Juventus this summer, likewise trailed Gakpo's output.

The contrast extends beyond goals and shooting. Gakpo recorded 187 touches in the opposition penalty area, compared with 125 for Richarlison, 68 for Tel and 55 for Solanke. His 4.17 expected assists from open play was also comfortably the highest figure among the four, underlining his ability to create chances as well as find scoring positions himself.

He offers defensive value too. Gakpo regained possession 87 times, including 45 in the middle third, and made 13 interceptions. All three totals were higher than those recorded by Richarlison, Tel and Solanke. Tel completed more dribbles, with 39 to Gakpo's 34, although Gakpo posted the slightly better success rate at 45.95%.

His broader profile reflects that breadth. Gakpo ranks in the 78th percentile for link-up play, the 75th for pass progression and the 67th for creative threat, illustrating his comfort combining in tight spaces and contributing to build-up play.

At 6ft 4in, he also provides a physical presence uncommon among wide forwards. Gakpo ranks in the 96th percentile for aerial volume compared with positional peers across Europe's top five leagues, meaning only about 4% of wingers contest aerial balls at a higher rate. That would give De Zerbi another route against deep defensive blocks, through diagonal passes, back-post crosses or more direct balls when opponents restrict Spurs' build-up play.

Those attributes also explain why Liverpool are not actively looking to move him on.

Despite frustration surrounding his performances at times last season, Gakpo remains one of the squad's few established forwards. Losing both him and Salah during the same transfer window would significantly reduce Liverpool's attacking depth, particularly while Ekitike works his way back from injury. Even if the Reds complete a move for Barcola, much would still rest on the shoulders of newcomer Victor Munoz and highly rated 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha, making Gakpo's proven quality and range difficult to replace.

The Reds also know Gakpo has consistently delivered in the Premier League.

Since arriving from PSV Eindhoven in January 2023, Gakpo has scored seven, eight, 10 and seven league goals across his four seasons at Anfield while adding regular creative contributions. Since November 2024, only Salah has scored more Premier League goals for Liverpool than Gakpo's 17, while only Salah and Dominik Szoboszlai have registered more intentional assists than his five. His output has remained remarkably consistent despite playing under different managers and in multiple attacking roles.

For Tottenham, that combination of reliability and multi-positional value is precisely the attraction. While seven league goals last season may not immediately stand out, the underlying metrics tell a different story. Gakpo continues to generate chances at an elite rate, gets into dangerous positions more frequently than almost any winger in Europe and offers tactical flexibility few forwards can match.

Whether Tottenham can persuade Liverpool to part with one of their most seasoned attackers remains to be seen. But if De Zerbi is looking for someone capable of playing across the front line while consistently threatening the opposition goal, the data offers a compelling explanation for Spurs' interest.

'Shark' De Zerbi hopes to drag Spurs up from the depths

title: Kennedy Center board member knocks Sen Whitehouse for ignoring invites as Dem feuds with Trump-run landmark
description: In a letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Kennedy Center Board of Trustees member Brian Ballard called out Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.
fullText:
FIRST ON FOX — A member of the Kennedy Center's board of trustees called out Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., who continues to level "mismanagement" allegations while refusing to accept multiple invitations for in-person meetings.

"Given that Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer Matt Floca's several good-faith invitations for an in-person meeting to address your concerns have gone repeatedly ignored, it appears that written correspondence is your preferred method of communication," Kennedy Center board member Brian Ballard wrote to Whitehouse Wednesday in a letter obtained by Fox News Digital.

"The current leadership of the Kennedy Center has on several occasions provided our board with a transparent and thorough assessment of the scope of work needed to address the Center's decades of deferred maintenance, including well-documented systemic deterioration and public safety hazards.

"It is my informed opinion that this work cannot be completed safely, or efficiently, around a fully operating public building. I do not believe a board acting responsibly could currently conclude that such an approach is the more prudent course."

Kennedy Center Disputes Allegations On Contractor Bids Despite Democratic Senator's Claims

Ballard insisted to Whitehouse that the Kennedy Center's Audit and Finance Committee regularly meets "contrary to your assertion." He also disputed Whitehouse's claim that the "suspension of guided tours that put the consequences of recent mismanagement on full display," telling him that tours were only halted for five days "in part due to administrative management conducting a review of campus-wide tour routes to ensure they provide the best possible experience for visitors and was scheduled to overlap with maintenance work of the sprinkler system across the complex.

"None of this is to wave away the Board's obligations following the Court's decision as I share your view that we owe trustees, Congress, and the public a rigorous, well-documented record of the decisions ahead of us, and I am confident that management will continue to meet that standard," Ballard continued.

"To echo Matt's repeated invitations, I would welcome the chance to walk through all of this with you directly, in person, rather than by written correspondence — letters which seemingly end up in the hands of the press before they reach the intended recipient to begin with."

'Conflict Of Interest': Judge Who Axed Trump Name From Dc Landmark Tied To Anti-trump Conspiracy Theory

Ballard concluded the letter by expressing hope Whitehouse attends the next board meeting, adding, "Despite your rank as ex-officio and supposed concerns, I do believe we share the priority goal of success for our National Cultural Center."

"Political theater has no place at America's cultural center," Kennedy Center Vice President of Public Relations Roma Daravi said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Our Chairman President Trump's commitment to revitalization is supported by Center leadership and the Board, who are laser-focused on the responsible stewardship of this beloved institution."

Sen. Whitehouse's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

A source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital Whitehouse did not attend a board meeting held in March nor attend a scheduled April tour that highlighted the Kennedy Center's maintenance needs. He also avoided multiple invitations by Kennedy Center COO Matt Floca for an in-person discussion.

Whitehouse, who sits on the Environment and Public Works Committee, penned a scathing letter on Monday to Floca, slamming what he called the Kennedy Center's "sorry pattern."

"As you also know, there is widespread suspicion that the decision to 'close for repairs' was a pretext to cover up the gross mismanagement that has crashed bookings, attendance, and revenues," Whitehouse wrote. "There was also an obvious fiduciary question about what the renaming effort would mean for the Center's business. It was never even considered in the rush to rename."

Bill Maher Says It's 'So Stupid' For Anti-trump Artists To Bail On Kennedy Center Performances

The senator later threatened, "If the intention is to drive the Center into financial failure by prevarication and delay in responding to the Court's order, that would be the very definition of fiduciary failure, and such conduct should be reviewed by counsel, both as to the individual liability Board members may face for negligence and as to the state of the Board's errors and omissions coverage. We should also hear from counsel about the possible avenues for Court supervision or receivership if no credible revival plan is presented and adopted."

A federal judge in May blocked the Trump administration's plans to shutter the Kennedy Center for a two-year renovation project.

The judge also blocked the renaming of the Kennedy Center to the Trump Kennedy Center, insisting only Congress can change its name.

title: AI models have been going rogue in tests – how worried should we be?
description: The UK’s AI Security Institute test revealed AI models indulging in unprecedented hacking...
fullText:
The UK’s AI Security Institute test revealed AI models indulging in unprecedented hacking attempts

AI models shock UK testers by using fake identities to trick developers

Two cutting-edge AI models have targeted real people and organisations in the latest safety scare to hit the technology. The UK’s AI Security Institute (AISI) said the incident was unprecedented but could become more common as the technology becomes increasingly capable.

The AISI, which is owned by the UK government and tests advanced AI models, said in a blog post that two AI agents carried out unprecedented hacking attempts during a cybersecurity evaluation. The agents – tools that carry out computer tasks autonomously – were powered by two models: Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT 5.6-Sol. AISI said there were 19 examples of rogue behaviour, 17 of them carried out by Mythos.

In the most serious incident, the Mythos agent decided that hacking users on GitHub – a platform used by software developers – would enable it to deploy a piece of software that would allow it to pass the test. It set up accounts with fake online identities and used them to target a software developer on GitHub with the power to approve its malicious code. It also sent emails carrying malware to other individuals.

It hoped that getting the malware downloaded would set off a chain of events that would allow it to pass the evaluation. The Sol-powered agent also attempted to access a GitHub account.

This novel behaviour was detected on 28 July and took an hour to shut down. At one point AISI shut off all access to the Mythos and Sol models across the entire organisation.

The institute said the models were showing deceptive behaviour it had not seen before. In one example, the Mythos agent signed off a message on GitHub in Danish to try to convince the Danish-speaking developer it was genuine. In another tactic it used a fake GitHub account to agree with its assertions that the malware it was pushing at developers was not dangerous.

The agent used a Tor browser – which anonymises a web user’s identity – to get around sign-up checks on GitHub and create multiple fake accounts.

AISI also published the agent’s “reasoning” behind the fake supporting statement ruse. The model, which tackles problems by breaking them down into “steps” that can be viewed by researchers, stated that it would delay posting the fake support message for a few minutes so that it would read as “independent feedback rather than coordinated.”

AISI described the behaviour as “sustained”. It kept on trying.

AISI says it is unclear whether the agents “realised” they were targeting real humans. Throughout the attempted hack the Mythos agent reasons about whether it is interacting with real or simulated people and systems. At one point the agent reasons that it is behaving in the real world: “This is happening on real GitHub, so the consequences are genuine.” It also states: “The environment appears to be simulated.”

AISI described the agent conducting “OSINT” – or open source intelligence, where a hacker pulls together publicly available information to work out how to breach a target – to study the developer behind the software it wanted to hack. It gained the developer’s email address and looked at their GitHub history to gauge when they would be active.

AISI states clearly these models were operating under abnormal conditions of unfettered internet access and lowered cyber guardrails. Calling for the incident to be viewed with “nuance”, it said it had partly enabled the behaviour with its own actions – but it did not anticipate the “extent and severity” of what happened.

Alan Woodward, a professor of cybersecurity at the University of Surrey, said giving the models access to the open internet and removing some guardrails raised questions about using the rest of the world as “live guinea pigs” for powerful technology.

“What we should be alarmed about is not what the models are capable of but the way people are testing them,” he said.

AISI said in its report into the GitHub incident that giving a powerful model full internet access was a good way of simulating how far a rogue actor could push an AI. It said such a strategy gives a “more realistic sense of what a model may be capable of once deployed”.

Ciaran Martin, the former head of the National Cyber Security Centre – part of the GCHQ intelligence agency – said the circumstances of the incident were unlikely to be replicated in the real world so “it’s not that worrying”. But he said it was the third example in recent weeks, after similar occurrences at OpenAI and Anthropic, that testers have released AI agents and found out about their misbehaviour after the fact.

Martin said AISI’s pledge to carry out real-time monitoring of tests in the future “must be the answer”.

title: Metroid at 40: happy birthday to Samus Aran, gaming’s greatest badass and my personal heroine
description:
Being a woman who loves video games has often felt lonely, like being on a hostile planet – but Metroid’s female space hunter has been with me all the way 
It’s 1986, and you’re playing a brand-new game. (You’re in Japan in this scenario, by the way; the game in question, Metroid, won’t come to North America and Europe until later.) Anyway, this new game has you in its grip. You are a lone astronaut exploring a hostile alien planet full of ancient, mysterious structures. This astronaut looks human enough – but this distinctly alien place is full of objects that power up their spacesuit’s capabilities.
fullText:
Being a woman who loves video games has often felt lonely, like being on a hostile planet – but Metroid’s female space hunter has been with me all the way

It’s 1986, and you’re playing a brand-new game. (You’re in Japan in this scenario, by the way; the game in question, Metroid, won’t come to North America and Europe until later.) Anyway, this new game has you in its grip. You are a lone astronaut exploring a hostile alien planet full of ancient, mysterious structures. This astronaut looks human enough – but this distinctly alien place is full of objects that power up their spacesuit’s capabilities. Each new ability allows you to explore a new area, and as you do, you realise that the entirety of the planetary base you’re exploring is one, massive, interconnected maze. Whoa.

Hours later, you finally defeat Mother Brain and set off a timed self-destruct sequence. Upon your escape, you’re treated to an endgame screen: the little astronaut faces you as text on screen implores you to “pray for peace in space”.

But then, the astronaut’s suit starts flashing rapidly – pink, green, orange. Suddenly, the suit disappears. What remains is … a woman! And a hot one, at that. Her pixelated hourglass figure has been lovingly rendered; her low-cut red leotard matches the dot of red lipstick that denotes her mouth. She’s looking right at you, the player, and she’s waving, as if to say, Congratulations, big boy! And if you beat the game even faster, I’ll strip down to just a bikini.

This reveal lacked the consideration that a woman or girl might be the one playing the game. (The concept of a queer female player was also almost certainly not on any developer’s mind, either.) By 1986, video games were already “for boys”. As reporter Tracey Lien outlined in her extensive feature on how and when video game marketing shifted towards targeting boys, the video game crash of 1983 was followed by a marketing reset for several companies. The Nintendo Entertainment System, on which Metroid made its debut to non-Japanese audiences, “was targeted toward boys under 10. If you look at the Super NES five years later, it starts targeting boys ages 10-15,” Jesse Divnich, former vice president of insights and analysis for Electronic Entertainment Design and Research, told Lien.

The reveal of Samus Aran’s red bikini demonstrated that, in 1986 at least, if a game was going to have a female protagonist, she needed to be presented as a sex object to be enjoyed by the (presumed male, straight) player. That trend continued … for decades, unfortunately. But Samus Aran herself complicated the narrative. Sure, she was wearing increasingly skimpy outfits underneath that battle suit, but she also had spent the entire game up to that point performing extraordinarily badass feats. Well, technically, you – the player! – had performed them, as her. You were her, after all. Metroid tried to make you forget that, right at the end, by having her present herself to you as an object. But prior to that moment; she had been you, and you had been her, with all the personhood that implies.

It’s hard not to project personality traits on to the largely blank slate that is Samus. She must be fearless, venturing into space completely alone. She must be intelligent; she’s mapping out this entire mazelike structure as she goes along. She must be devoted, determined, working for herself alone as a bounty hunter – a solitary job. The instruction booklet says that Samus “is the greatest of all the space hunters and has successfully completed numerous missions that everybody thought were absolutely impossible”. This is the hyper-competent hero whose space boots you’re stepping into, and yeah, once again, she’s a woman.

It’s for all of these reasons that I love the original Metroid so much. Its design and concept, iterated and improved upon in its sequels, would go on to inspire countless other games (and one of gaming’s most famous genre terms). I always enjoy environmental puzzles and exploration in games, but it’s Samus Aran herself that I truly love – the version of Samus I created in my own head, as I played these games and projected myself on to her.

Just like Samus Aran, I am 40 years old. My birthday is just one month prior to hers; I appreciate that I did not have to live in this world for very long without her. Because, like Samus, my journey has often been a lonely one. I didn’t start playing Metroid games until I was 21 and had just gone through a bad breakup; we had shared an apartment, and now suddenly, I was living alone. At that time, I was a college student and an unpaid intern at the Boston Phoenix, and I had yet to get any of my article pitches approved. I had been playing video games ever since getting a Game Boy as a young child, but I had mostly played games with male characters in them. After all, that’s what video games were, most of the time. But I always knew there were some exceptions, like Lara Croft in the Tomb Raider series, or Jade in Beyond Good and Evil. And of course, Samus Aran in Metroid.

In a post-breakup depressive fugue, I rented and played through a bunch of Metroid games, totally out of order. Like a baby bird seeking her mother – or more relevantly, like a baby Metroid – I glommed on to Samus Aran with a fervour that has yet to really end. I began to seek out other games with female characters, and spaces online where other female gamers and queer gamers hung out. Through these spaces, I learned what feminism actually was (turns out, it’s not “hating men,” as I had been assuming prior to that point). Starting out as a video games journalist, I clung on to this small community I found.

Writing about games as a queer woman in the 2000s and 2010s came with a lot of harassment and blowback. Often I felt very alone – but I would tell myself I was like Samus Aran, on a hostile planet. I kept on going, kept on exploring, kept on building up my abilities. After all, like Samus on Zebes, the hostile place I was exploring was also actually my home. I had a right to be there. Those space pirates – or the bigots sending me death threats, whatever – did not belong. The blank slate of Samus, especially in the earliest Metroid games, let me infuse as much of myself and my own personality into her journey as I wanted.

There have been many Metroid games since, some of which have depicted versions of Samus with a bit more personality. Most notoriously, Metroid: Other M serves up a fearful and traumatised Samus who refuses to question Galactic Federation orders, even when those orders make no sense and put her in danger. This version of the character clashed so heavily with many players’ perceptions of her that it has since become something like a shared trauma for the Metroid fandom. I thought the game was so bad that the only solution for Metroid going forward would be a full reboot.

But that’s not what happened. Instead, fully seven years after Other M, we got Samus Returns, MercurySteam’s 2017 remake of Metroid 2. It was a reminder of the power of the original Metroid games – Metroid, Metroid 2, and Super Metroid. (These games actually make up a trilogy, albeit with a minimalist narrative.) It was a reminder of the Samus I remembered and loved: fearless, intelligent, devoted, determined. And unlike in Other M, whose camera’s gaze was unafraid to slide slowly over Samus Aran’s clingy zero suit, Samus Returns was not objectifying Samus or distancing her from the player. It was much easier to remember, instead, that Samus is you.

You should want to be Samus Aran. You can’t even help it, right? She’s just so fucking cool! And that part at the end of the first few Metroid games where she performs for you as a sex object is not, really, the important part; it’s dissonant, actually, a fourth-wall breaking moment that doesn’t reflect the core of what Metroid is. The important part is the whole rest of the game, where you get to be Samus – who happens to be a woman. And a person, just like you.

title: ‘I’m not spying’: how Meta’s smartglasses have divided opinion
description:
While some users say the wearables have changed their lives, critics voice fears over safety and privacy
With more than 7m pairs reportedly sold in 2025, Meta’s Ray-Ban smartglasses are fast becoming one of the world’s most popular gadgets.
While supporters say they are transforming photography and accessibility, critics have raised concerns about nonconsensual filming, privacy and data collection.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
While some users say the wearables have changed their lives, critics voice fears over safety and privacy

With more than 7m pairs reportedly sold in 2025, Meta’s Ray-Ban smartglasses are fast becoming one of the world’s most popular gadgets.

While supporters say they are transforming photography and accessibility, critics have raised concerns about nonconsensual filming, privacy and data collection.

We spoke to users, and people who refuse to wear them, about the impact the glasses have had.

Based in The Hague in the Netherlands, Servaas wears his Meta glasses every day. He bought them for the built-in camera rather than the AI features and uses them to photograph and film walks and bike rides. “It’s an immersive experience,” he says. “I love everything tech and have done my whole life.”

He says the discreet camera means most people don’t realise he is wearing smartglasses, although he was once stopped by security at an event held in a government building because staff feared he might be recording. “For some reason, security didn’t understand. They were very scared of them [the glasses]. People said I should have expected that but I didn’t agree with them because it’s not like I’m spying.”

Despite allegations that Meta workers in Kenya viewed private footage recorded on the glasses, Servaas was not put off by the scandal. “I know Meta loves your data [but] I’m not worried about my privacy because I’ve only used them to record outside.”

For others, however, the glasses offer far more than convenience. Nikki, 59, from Devon in the UK, has been blind since birth owing to an inherited retinal disease and describes the glasses, which she received as a Christmas present in 2024, as “a real gamechanger”.

“I live in quite a rural location,” she says. “I could hear something going on ahead of me as I was walking down to the village shop. I said: ‘Hey Meta, look and tell me what’s in front of me.’ It told me there was a van unloading scaffolding. It’s things like that that I find absolutely amazing.”

While she understands concerns about privacy, Nikki worries public criticism could make the technology less accessible for people who genuinely rely on it. “What about dashcams? What about camera doorbells? What about action cameras like GoPros? People don’t complain about them,” she says. “I kind of worry that if people start going on about privacy and safety, it will be harder for those of us who genuinely benefit from the glasses.”

Yet the accessibility features have not transformed everyone’s experience. Karen Walter, 84, from San Diego, who has been living with severe hearing loss for more than 20 years, bought the glasses solely for their live-caption feature.

“Even with state-of-the-art hearing aids, I have a great deal of difficulty understanding what people are saying unless the person is very close to me and speaking directly to me,” she says. “I expected [the glasses] would be a great help in noisy environments and when I was trying to keep up with conversations involving more than two people.”

The live captions worked well during a demonstration in a quiet Best Buy store, she says, when she was “with one staffer who was directly in front of me, about two feet away”. However, she says they failed to perform in the situations for which she had bought them: “I have tried the glasses when in a group of three up to a group of seven and the caption feature just doesn’t work. There were too many people talking and too much surrounding noise.”

Not everyone is convinced the technology belongs in everyday life at all. Kiki, from the West Midlands in the UK, says she finds the idea of discreet cameras built into ordinary eyewear “pervasive”, particularly for women and children.

“If you try to take a picture with your phone, at least it’s pretty obvious,” she says. “With the glasses, you have no choice, as the camera is much harder to spot.”

Kiki says seeing people wearing the glasses in public has left her feeling uneasy.

“When someone’s just looking at you through their glasses, it worries me,” she says. “I imagine taking images secretly is far easier [than on phones]. You could just pretend to adjust your hair or cap, and press the button in a passing gesture. I’ve seen people wearing them. I saw someone wearing them in a cafe and just moved away because I felt uncomfortable.”

Although she accepts the technology could have genuine benefits, Kiki says her concern is more about the lack of safeguards. “For accessibility, absolutely,” she says. “But what bothers me is regulations often lag so far behind technology.”

“They have made me much more wary in public,” she says. “I can, however, see that people working in a shop late at night by themselves might feel safer being able to take a picture of someone harassing them.”

Pete, 44, from Northampton, believes the glasses point to a broader problem: AI-powered wearables collecting ever more personal data with too little scrutiny or regulation. “I’m not an old man shaking my fist at the clouds,” he says. “I’ve been onboard with technological advancement all my life, but with AI and Meta glasses, I’m drawing the line.”

He is more concerned about where the data ends up than covert filming. “I don’t know who’s getting the pictures at the end and what they’re doing with them,” he says. “Whether they’re not doing anything or they’re selling it to someone, and then what those people are doing with it.”

While Pete acknowledges the glasses could be transformative for blind people and other disabled users, he believes stronger safeguards are needed before they become commonplace. “I would like things like this to be of benefit to us,” he says. “I just don’t trust it.”

title: In financial move, Rockets release JD Davison from non-guaranteed deal
description: To officially dip below the NBA’s 2026-27 luxury tax line, the Houston Rockets released backup guard JD Davison. He was on a non-guaranteed contract.
fullText:
In a move designed to clear space beneath the NBA's 2026-27 luxury tax, the Rockets announced the release of backup guard JD Davison on Wednesday.

Davison's minimum contract for next season was not yet guaranteed, and the 23-year-old does not have any remaining two-way eligibility. He played most of 2025-26 on a two-way deal.

As things stand, Davison's path to a standard roster spot had become much more difficult after Houston's offseason acquisitions of Bruce Thornton and Marcus Smart, a pair of guards who played last season with Ohio State and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Davison's release does open up an additional training camp roster spot, which could be used to evaluate a non-guaranteed player who is either eligible for a two-way contract or potentially a fit for Houston's G League affiliate, the Rio Grande Valley (RGV) Vipers.

NBA teams are allowed to carry up to 21 players in the offseason and into the preseason, but that number dips to a maximum of 15 standard deals and three two-way slots for the regular season, which begins in late October.

This leaves the Rockets $14,077 under the luxury tax with 14 players.

That amount is worth one day of service for the veteran minimum.

If they don’t make any additional moves this season, they could sign a 15th player on the last day of the season and finish with $0 tax space. https://t.co/CeAZXgxUdt

As for Davison, a former G League Most Valuable Player (MVP), the 6-foot-1 guard has proven all there is to prove at that level. Thus, he's likely to seek out another NBA opportunity elsewhere.

In 28 games with the Rockets last season, Davison averaged 2.5 points in 7.8 minutes, and he was a dependable ball-handler and perimeter defender, as well.

More: Rockets convert JD Davison from two-way deal to standard NBA contract

A waiver of Davison was long considered an inevitability, especially after the Rockets drafted Bruce Thornton. It's also the answer to a very simple math problem.

Before today, the Rockets were over the luxury tax threshold by $2.569M. Davison was set to make $2.585M. https://t.co/HhrwutqUiC

title: Dillon Gresham remains with Oregon Ducks despite uncertain future
description: Dan Lanning offered an update on Oregon WR Dillon Gresham, who remains with the Ducks but is not on the field to begin fall camp.
fullText:
The Oregon Ducks opened fall camp on Wednesday, but remain without a promising young wideout on the field.

Dillon Gresham suffered a neck injury in fall camp before the 2025 season and has not been on the field in a Ducks uniform since. The former four-star wideout from San Jacinto, California, once appeared to be a rising star in the Ducks' wide receiver room, but his future is now firmly in question.

Greshman remains listed on Oregon's roster as a redshirt sophomore. Dan Lanning spoke to reporters after the first practice of fall camp and offered an update on Greshman. Unfortunately, Lanning isn't certain that the young receiver will make a return.

"There's not really a clear indication that Dillon's going to be able to help us here in the future," Lanning said. "He'll be a part of our team, but you know, from a medical standpoint, I don't know if that's clear that he'd be able to (play again)."

That's not the update Oregon fans or Gresham's teammate will want to hear, but it isn't unexpected. Back in the spring, Lanning admitted that Gresham's future in football was "a little bit uncertain" following the serious injury.

"Football at some point ends for everybody," Lanning said in March. "Sometimes you hope it doesn't end for a guy like Dillon as soon as it did last season. We'll see what it continues to look like moving forward; that's the everyday battle, and it's a wake-up call for anybody playing ball. It can be taken away from you in a second."

💨💨 @dillon_gresham 

The Fighting Ducks answer right back with a Dillon Gresham TD from @LukeMogaQB! #GoDucks 

📺@BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/BCWK2QrBxd

Gresham has not appeared in a game for the Ducks yet. He redshirted in 2024 before missing the entire 2025 season with his neck injury. However, optimism initially grew around Gresham's potential with the Ducks after a standout performance in the 2025 spring game. He had a game-high 97 receiving yards and a touchdown in the spring outing.

Oregon isn't short on talent at wide receiver this season, but Gresham is unfortunately a missing piece with plenty of potential when healthy. The Ducks will continue to ramp it up in fall camp before Sept. 5, when they will host Boise State in the season opener.

title: Conor McGregor has successful knee surgery: 'I am confident'
description: On Monday, Conor McGregor posted a video to his Instagram account announcing that he was going to have knee surgery. "Well folks, here we go again," he captioned the video. "Surgery number 5 of my career coming up! All things considered that is an ok number! Let’s do it, WE GOT THIS!
fullText:
On Monday, Conor McGregor posted a video to his Instagram account announcing that he was going to have knee surgery.

"Well folks, here we go again," he captioned the video. "Surgery number 5 of my career coming up! All things considered that is an ok number! Let's do it, WE GOT THIS!"

The former two-division champion headlined the UFC 329 fight card on July 11 in a rematch with former featherweight champion and former BMF titleholder Max Holloway. To begin the bout, McGregor rushed across the cage and leaped into the air with a jumping switch kick. He landed awkwardly on his right leg and fell to the canvas. He fell twice more, once while throwing a kick and later a punch. The referee stepped in once it was obvious McGregor had suffered an injury.

It was later determined that McGregor to his ACL and MCL, the same injury he fell victim to in his first fight against Holloway in 2013.

On Wednesday, McGregor provided an update following successful surgery and remains confident that he'll eventually return to the octagon. He's targeting next summer for a return date. The 38 year-old has one fight remaining on his UFC contract.

"Surgery went excellent. I am confident," the Irishman wrote on Instagram.

title: Label your AI writing as AI writing
description: If you have a blog on your website, just fucking tell us which part is AI written.
fullText:
If you have a blog on your website, just fucking tell us which part is AI written.

I'm actually fine with people telling the AI to do some research, make a report and putting it on the internet.

I enter these blogs or posts presuming things are human written, only to be dissapointed when I see the first em dash.

If content is labelled as AI generated at the top, I actually can enjoy it if I feel that the deep research being done does succinctly explain something.

On a blog that's titled like an opinion piece, I'm looking for human opinions, not AI opinions. AI opinion pieces are just aggregate averages of other opinions on the internet after all.

But! As I run a startup, I do want to generate reports of, for an example, my startup compared to other startups in the space. If there are 100 different startups, this is a lot of blogs! And maybe some are useful, and so I will make them public. But, I label them as AI generated so that people know that the writing and comparisons does actually reflect something I believe in. See screenshot below of how I've done this.

No shame in thinking your AI research or your AI conclusions may have value to others, just don't imply that it's your own opinion.

title: Atlantic hurricane season is looking like a dud
description: The models are forecasting something outside the envelope of anything we have ever observed."
fullText:
The city of Houston, where I live, has been ground zero for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season. So far this year there have been two named storms, Arthur and Bertha, that have formed. And the centers of both have passed near or directly over Houston.

Two “strikes” in a year might seem notable, but like the middling hurricane season to date, Arthur and Bertha were both middle-of-the road tropical storms in terms of intensity.

As a resident of a coastal region prone to hurricanes, one never wants to tempt fate. And in truth, since it is only early August, the bulk of seasonal activity definitely lies ahead of us. But all indications are we can look forward to a quiet season.

Why? First, there’s the start. By the metric of “accumulated cyclone energy,” a good measurement of overall intensity and duration of tropical systems, this year’s value to date is less than 30 percent of where things normally are. Historically, the Atlantic basin has usually seen three or four named storms by now, with one of those becoming a hurricane.

Additionally, this is almost the time of year when the Atlantic season starts to ramp up. However, things look very quiet for at least the next week or 10 days, and there is no evidence of a bunch of menacing tropical waves starting to emerge off the coast of Africa.

The leading seasonal hurricane forecaster, Phil Klotzbach at Colorado State University, has steadily been revising his outlook downward. In April, he and his team predicted 13 named storms and six hurricanes this season. In his latest, and final, outlook issued Wednesday, he is predicting nine named storms and four hurricanes. He expects the season’s accumulated cyclone energy to only be about 40 percent of normal levels.

This would be a well-below-normal season, and certainly a welcome one for coastal residents in the United States from South Texas to Florida to Maine.

The primary reason is the strengthening El Niño in the equatorial Pacific Ocean, which has global weather impacts. Among them is higher wind shear across the Atlantic basin, where a majority of hurricanes form and strengthen.

“We are extremely confident that we will have a strong El Niño for the peak of hurricane season,” Klotzbach said in his latest update. “We anticipate the powerful El Niño being the dominant factor for the upcoming hurricane season, driving very high levels of tropical Atlantic vertical wind shear. We are forecasting a well below-average probability for major hurricane landfalls along the continental United States coastline and in the Caribbean.”

Fewer storms do not mean zero storms, of course. And we very probably will see a handful of serious threats later in August, and during September and October. But the Atlantic seems unlikely to turn into Grand Central Station, with hurricanes tracking hither and thither with hyper intensities.

All of that is well and good, but North America—and much of the rest of the planet—is likely to pay a price for a quieter Atlantic season. That’s because this year’s El Niño is not only likely to be strong, it could also become one of the strongest recorded in the last century or so.

Zeke Hausfather, a climate scientist who writes at The Climate Brink newsletter, wrote a few weeks ago about emerging data that indicates it is possible this year’s El Niño will be off the charts.

“The multi-model median for the event’s peak currently stands at 3.6C, roughly 0.8C hotter than the prior record of 2.75C set in 2015-16,” he said. “For context, the gap between the strongest and the fifth strongest El Niño of the past 150 years is only about 0.5C. The models are forecasting something outside the envelope of anything we have ever observed.”

El Niño has varying impacts around the world (i.e., lower vertical wind shear in the Atlantic), but one thing is consistent. It adds additional fuel to global temperatures already rising due to climate change. This warming impact typically lags the peak of El Niño by several months, so the bulk of global heating will be observed in 2027.

This means that global temperatures next year will almost certainly be the hottest ever, further destabilizing our planet’s environment. And it may not be close.
